PURPOSE:THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO INCREASE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT LOCAL WEATHER SYSTEMS IN THE LOWER ATMOSPHERE, ENABLING THE SAFE INTEGRATION OF SMALL UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES AND ADVANCED AIR MOBILITY AIRCRAFT INTO THE NATIONAL AIRSPACE SYSTEM.ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED:THE RESEARCHERS WILL CREATE A METHOD TO STANDARDIZE AND TRACE COMMERCIAL UAS AND ADVANCED AIR MOBILITY (AAM) ATMOSPHERIC MEASUREMENTS. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP PROTOCOLS AND STANDARDS FOR THE UNMANNED AIRCRAFT METEOROLOGICAL DATA REPORT. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO EVALUATE EXISTING MAINTENANCE OPERATIONS THAT MAY SUPPORT AAM OPERATIONS, PARTICULARLY RELATED TO WEATHER IMPACTS RELATED TO SEVERE WEATHER AND FIRE. THE RESEARCHERS WILL ALSO DEVELOP CURRICULA TO HELP THE AVIATION COMMUNITY APPLY THE NEW TECHNOLOGY.EXPECTED OUTCOMES:THIS PROJECT WILL DEMONSTRATE A NOVEL, COST-EFFECTIVE METHOD TO SUPPORT THE INTEGRATION OF WEATHER SENSORS IN COMMERCIAL UAS AND AAM AIRCRAFT. THE PROPOSED SYSTEM IS ESSENTIAL FOR GATHERING LOCAL WEATHER DATA AND ESTABLISHING A WEATHER INFORMATION DISSEMINATION NETWORK. THE PROJECT WILL DEMONSTRATE DYNAMIC PATH PLANNING BASED ON LOCAL WEATHER DATA.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES:THIS PROJECT FACILITATES THE SAFE AND SUSTAINABLE INTEGRATION OF SMALL UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS AND ADVANCED AIR MOBILITY INTO THE NATIONAL AIRSPACE SYSTEM. THE TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCEMENTS WILL ALSO BENEFIT THE BROADER AVIATION COMMUNITY. THE ENHANCED COVERAGE AND PRECISION OF LOW-ALTITUDE WEATHER DATA OFFER SIGNIFICANT BENEFITS TO THE HELICOPTER-BASED EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES COMMUNITY OPERATING WITHIN THE SAME AIRSPACE, HELPING TO MITIGATE THEIR OPERATIONAL RISKS. THE METEOROLOGY COMMUNITY WILL BE ABLE TO LEVERAGE THIS DATA TO REFINE WEATHER PRODUCTS AND EXTEND WARNING TIMES FOR POTENTIALLY HAZARDOUS CONDITIONS CONTRIBUTING TO SAFETY MEASURES FOR VARIOUS STAKEHOLDERS WITHIN THE AIRSPACE ECOSYSTEM.SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES:THE RECIPIENT PLANS TO SUB-AWARD FUNDS FOR CONSULTING SERVICES TO PROVIDE ENGINEERING SUPPORT AND DATA ANALYSIS.

PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS GRANT IS TO HELP DEVELOP AND VALIDATE STANDARD TEST METHODS FOR SMALL UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS (AKA DRONES) USED BY PUBLIC SAFETY AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE ORGANIZATIONS. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: THE GRANTEE WILL HOST TEST METHOD VALIDATION EXERCISES WITH EMERGENCY RESPONDERS TO CAPTURE FEEDBACK AND PERFORMANCE DATA WITHIN THE TEST METHODS AND RELATED OPERATIONAL SCENARIOS. THEY WILL ALSO PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE AND GUIDANCE FROM A VARIETY OF PUBLIC SAFETY AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE ORGANIZATIONS INTERESTED IN USING SUCH STANDARDS TO SUPPORT PURCHASING DECISIONS, FOCUS TRAINING, AND EVALUATE LEVELS OF REMOTE PILOT PROFICIENCY FOR CREDENTIALING. THESE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS WILL HELP PRIORITIZE TEST METHODS FOR THE STANDARDIZATION PROCESS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THIS GRANT WILL PRODUCE A SERIES OF STANDARD TEST METHODS FOR BALLOTING THROUGH THE ASTM INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS COMMITTEE ON HOMELAND SECURITY APPLICATIONS; RESPONSE ROBOTS (E54.09). ALSO, POTENTIALLY NEW USE CASES FROM PUBLIC SAFETY AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE ORGANIZATIONS WITH THRESHOLDS OF ACCEPTABLE PERFORMANCE IN EACH TEST METHOD FOR VARIOUS AIRCRAFT BASED ON THEIR INTENDED MISSIONS, AIRSPACE RESTRICTIONS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: THE BENEFICIARIES WILL BE PUBLIC SAFETY AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE ORGANIZATIONS NATIONWIDE WHO WILL USE THE RESULTING TEST METHODS TO GUIDE PROCUREMENTS AND TRAIN WITH MEASURES OF REMOTE PILOT PROFICIENCY. THE PUBLIC WILL ALSO BENEFIT AS EMERGENCY RESPONSE ORGANIZATIONS BECOME EQUIPPED WITH BETTER LIFE-SAVING TOOLS AND TACTICS, ALONG WITH STANDARDS-BASED CREDENTIALING THAT WILL FACILITATE MUTUAL AID AT LARGE SCALE DISASTERS. SUSTAINABLE AND RESILIENT AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS NEW PROGRAMS, LIKE OUR AGRICULTURAL INNOVATION CENTER, INTEND TO BRING RESILIENCY TO THE FOOD SYSTEM WITH ENTREPRENEURSHIP. AND OUR LONG-SUCCESSFUL PROGRAMS LIKE INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, GRAZING SCHOOLS, SHOW-ME-SELECT REPLACEMENT HEIFERS, AGRICULTURAL LENDERS SCHOOL, AND SO MANY OTHERS WILL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE BEST-IN-CLASS EXTENSION EDUCATION. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES (SOLUTION-BASED) THAT ADDRESS FOOD SYSTEM RESILIENCY ISSUES ARE DEVELOPING DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES TO REDUCE THE LABOR AND NUMBER OF ENTITIES BETWEEN FOOD PRODUCERS AND CONSUMERS; AND TRAINING FOR FARMERS, FARM WORKERS, AND OTHERS IN THE FOOD SYSTEM ABOUT HOW TO USE THOSE TECHNOLOGIES. awards.Description: AS THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR HOMELAND SECURITY IN THE ARCTIC, THE ARCTIC DOMAIN AWARENESS CENTER (ADAC) WILL ADDRESS CHALLENGES ACROSS THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE (HSE), ADDING ARCTIC TO ITS NAME TO REPRESENT ITS EXPANDED STRATEGIC VISION. ADACARCTIC WILL DRAW ON ITS EXPERIENCE OPERATING THE PREVIOUS DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) ARCTIC REGIONAL CENTER TO CREATE AN INTERDISCIPLINARY NEXUS OF STRATEGIC LEADERS AND PARTNERS CAPABLE OF APPLYING EXPERTISE THROUGHOUT THE HSE. GUIDED BY ITS TEAM OF EXPERT RESEARCHERS, EDUCATORS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROFESSIONALS, TRANSFER AND TRANSITION EXPERTS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS, ADACARCTIC IS READY TO RESPOND TO THE CHALLENGES CONFRONTING DHS IN THE RAPIDLY CHANGING ARCTIC DOMAIN. VISION: ADDRESSING RAPID CHANGES THROUGH TECHNOLOGY, INNOVATION, AND COLLABORATION (ARCTIC).MISSION: CREATE TOOLS, TECHNOLOGIES, KNOWLEDGE PRODUCTS, AND HIGHLY QUALIFIED PERSONS THAT WILL SERVE THE HOMELAND SECURITY ENTERPRISE TO IMPROVE ARCTIC HOMELAND SECURITY.TO FULFILL ITS MISSION, THE CENTER WILL USE CUTTING-EDGE APPROACHES TO CONDUCT CRITICAL RESEARCH NEEDED TO PREPARE FOR AND IMPLEMENT AN EFFECTIVE RESPONSE TO THE CHALLENGES DHS FACES IN THE ARCTIC DOMAIN. IT WILL DO SO BY BRINGING TOGETHER AN ARRAY OF GEOGRAPHICALLY DISPERSED, STRATEGICALLY SELECTED PARTNERS FROM ACADEMIA, FEDERALLY-FUNDED RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CENTERS, INDUSTRY, NON-PROFITS, TRIBAL, AND OTHER FEDERAL, STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS WITH ARCTIC EXPERTISE. THROUGH THESE PARTNERSHIPS, ADACARCTIC WILL STIMULATE INNOVATIVE RESEARCH IDEAS AND PROJECTS, EXPAND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES, AND PROMOTE CENTER ENGAGEMENTS THAT PRODUCE TOOLS, TECHNOLOGIES, KNOWLEDGE PRODUCTS, AND TRAINED PERSONNEL. EACH PROJECT AND ACTIVITY WILL INVOLVE STUDENTS OR TRAINEES WHILE YIELDING A PRODUCT FOR TRANSFER AND TRANSITION, ALL TO EMPOWER HSE PERSONNEL AND SERVE THE DHS MISSION. ADACARCTICS SELECTED RESEARCH AND EDUCATION PROJECTS WILL CREATE STATE-OF-THE-ART TECHNOLOGIES TO FILL KNOWLEDGE GAPS AND SOLVE THE TOUGHEST CHALLENGES IN THE ARCTIC. THE SELECTED PROJECTS AIM TO TRANSITION TECHNOLOGY PRODUCTS THAT INCLUDE BUOYS AND DRONES TO MONITOR ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE FROM CHRONIC OR ACUTE CHANGES DISASTERS, TOOLS SUCH AS RISK ASSESSMENT EVALUATION METHODS FOR INFRASTRUCTURE AND METHODOLOGIES TO IMPROVE DECISION MAKING FOR RISK EVALUATORS AND RESPONDERS, MODELS FOR FAILED OIL WELL MANAGEMENT AND THE INTEGRATION OF A DIVERSE ENERGY PORTFOLIO, AND KNOWLEDGE PRODUCTS SUCH AS REFEREED PUBLICATIONS, LITERATURE REVIEWS, FEASIBILITY STUDIES, AND RAPPORT REPORTS. EDUCATIONAL, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT PROGRAMS INCLUDE AN INTEGRATED MULTI-INSTITUTION INTERDISCIPLINARY ARCTIC SECURITY GRADUATE DEGREE, A CENTER-LED ADACARCTIC STUDENT FELLOWSHIP PROGRAM INCORPORATING FELLOWS ON ACTIVE PROJECTS, TRIBAL ENGAGEMENT AND LIAISING, AND TRAINING PROGRAMS CREATED TO MEET SPECIFIC HSE NEEDS. THE KNOWLEDGE PRODUCTS WILL BE DISSEMINATED INTO THE SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE AND HSE THROUGH PAPERS, PRESENTATIONS, VIDEOS, AND WORKSHOPS COORDINATED AND PROMOTED BY THE CENTER. THE TECHNOLOGY PRODUCTS WILL BE TRANSFERRED AND TRANSITIONED TO DHS COMPONENTS AND INDUSTRIAL PARTNERS IN CLOSE COLLABORATION WITH THE UAA TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER OFFICE (TTO). MOREOVER, ADACARCTIC WILL CREATE AN ARCTIC TESTBED TO SUPPORT PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND FACILITATE UPTAKE AND TRANSITION TO PRACTICE BY CONDUCTING RIGOROUS, TRANSPARENT, AND REPLICABLE TESTING OF SCIENTIFIC THEORIES, COMPUTING TOOLS, AND NEW TECHNOLOGIES WHILE EMBRACING HARSH ARCTIC CONDITIONS AND CHALLENGES. THE DIVERSITY, COORDINATION, AND COLLABORATION OF ADACARCTIC AND ITS COLLABORATORS, AND ITS CLOSE PARTNERSHIPS WITH DHS AND THE HSE AT-LARGE, WILL YIELD FRESH IDEAS, EXEMPLARY PROJECT APPLICABILITY, AND EFFECTIVE TRANSITIONS, ALL TO THE BENEFIT OF THE HSE IN THE ARCTIC.

awards.Description: WEEDS ARE A KEY BIOTIC CONSTRAINT TO FARMERS. NOTWITHSTANDING, THERE HAS BEEN A NOTEWORTHY INCREASE IN HERBICIDE-RESISTANT WEEDS DUE TO PRACTICES THAT IMPOSE SELECTIVE PRESSURE ON WEED POPULATIONS. WE BELIEVE THAT COVER CROPS (CCS) CAN BE INSTRUMENTAL IN HELPING SOLVE THIS ISSUE VIA GREATER INCLUSION INTO INTEGRATED WEED MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES. THUS, OUR GOAL IS TO MORE EFFECTIVELY INCORPORATE CCS INTO WEED MANAGEMENT PLANS. WE FEEL THAT THIS CAN BE BEST ACCOMPLISHED BY HELPING VEGETABLE FARMERS REALIZE THEIR POTENTIAL BEYOND WEED SUPPRESSION. AS SUCH, ADDITIONAL SERVICES SUCH AS CCS POTENTIAL TO CUT INPUT COSTS, CONTRIBUTE FERTILITY, BIOREMEDIATE SOILS AND INFLUENCE NEMATODE COUNTS WILL BE EXAMINED. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO DEPLOY DRONES AND ROBOTS IN SUPPORT OF OUR FIVE MAIN OBJECTIVES WHICH ARE TO: 1) COMPARE DIFFERENT COVER CROPPING STRATEGIES FOR MANAGING WEEDS, 2) DETERMINE CC'S BELOW GROUND EFFECTS ON WEEDS, 3) DEVELOP COVER CROPPING TACTICS TO WORK ACROSS A BROAD RANGE OF CROPS, 4) EVALUATE THE PROFITABILITY OF GROWING VEGETABLES WITH CCS AND 5) DELIVER NEW CC INFORMATION TO END-USERS. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO ADDRESS THREE MAIN SCRI FOCUS AREAS AND OTHER USDA EMPHASIZED SPECIALTY CROP SECTORS' NEEDS: 1) ADDRESS THREATS FROM PESTS, 2) IMPROVE PRODUCTION EFFICIENCY, PRODUCTIVITY AND LONG-TERM PROFITABILITY, AND 3) RESEARCH NEW INNOVATIONS AND TECHNOLOGY (DRONES AND ROBOTS). IN ADDITION, THE TECHNOLOGY BEING RESEARCHED CAN BE USED TO REDUCE THE NEED FOR MANUAL LABOR WHICH WAS REQUESTED BY A NUMBER OF SPECIALTY CROP SECTORS. MOREOVER, THE NEXT GENERATION OF AG-PROFESSIONALS WILL BE INTRINSICALLY INVOLVED IN ALL PROJECT ASPECTS.

awards.Description: CENTER: NATIONAL CENTER FOR AUTONOMOUS TECHNOLOGIES ATE CENTER RENEWAL -IN 2018, THE MIT TECHNOLOGY REVIEW DEFINED EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES AS ?A TECHNOLOGY, OR PERHAPS EVEN A COLLECTION OF TECHNOLOGIES, THAT WILL HAVE A PROFOUND EFFECT ON OUR LIVES?. AUTONOMOUS TECHNOLOGIES (AT) FIT THAT DEFINITION. INNOVATIONS IN AT FOR AIR, LAND, AND SEA ARE HAVING A GLOBAL IMPACT ON: 1) THE ENVIRONMENT: LOWERING EMISSIONS, CARBON FOOTPRINTS, AND HELPING COMBAT CLIMATE CHANGE; 2) SOCIETY: REDUCING HUMAN RISKS IN EMERGENCY OPERATIONS, DELIVERING HEALTHCARE AND MEDICATIONS, IMPROVING RESOURCE ACCESS, AND ENHANCING SUPPLY CHAIN EFFICIENCY; AND 3) THE ECONOMY: CREATING EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES AND GROWING GNP. ACCORDING TO THE WORLD ECONOMIC FORUM AND CANN, AT WILL RESULT IN A NET EMPLOYMENT INCREASE OF 58 MILLION BY 2030, AND AUTONOMOUS VEHICLES ARE PROJECTED TO IMPACT THE US ECONOMY BY $4 TRILLION. THE NATIONAL CENTER FOR AUTONOMOUS TECHNOLOGIES (NCAT) WILL PROVIDE VALUABLE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES FOR TECHNICAL EDUCATION IN THIS RAPIDLY EVOLVING, HIGHLY DISRUPTIVE FIELD. NCAT'S LEADERSHIP AND COLLABORATIONS WITH AIR AND LAND STANDARDIZATION ORGANIZATIONS WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF CLEAR COMPETENCY MODELS, EFFECTIVE CREDENTIALS, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT ROADMAPS FOR ACCESSIBLE PATHWAYS IN AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE CAREERS INCLUDING DRONES, SELF-DRIVING CARS, AND MARITIME EXPLORATION. NCAT WILL BUILD CAPACITY ACROSS EXTENSIVE NETWORKS THROUGH THE FOLLOWING GOALS: 1) LEAD: EVOLVE AND FORTIFY PARTNERSHIPS AND COLLABORATIONS WITH STANDARDS ORGANIZATIONS DEFINING TECHNICIAN EDUCATION, TRAINING PROGRAMS, AND INDUSTRY-RECOGNIZED CERTIFICATIONS; 2) INSPIRE: ADVANCE STUDENT COMPETITION AND EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING FRAMEWORKS TO FACILITATE THE CONNECTIONS BETWEEN STUDENT ENGAGEMENT AND THE IMPACT ON WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT; 3) CONNECT: EXTEND THE NATIONAL COMMUNITY AND SUPPORT NETWORKS THAT FOSTER INNOVATIVE INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT AND EDUCATIONAL COLLABORATIONS TO ADVANCE AT TECHNICIAN EDUCATION PROGRAMS, INCLUDING WORK-BASED LEARNING (WBL) INITIATIVES; AND 4) SERVE: EXPAND THE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCE HUB WITH A FOCUS ON LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY AND ACCESS TO RESOURCES FOR COMMUNITY COLLABORATORS AND PARTNERS ACROSS ALL AT IN THE AIR, LAND AND SEA DOMAINS OF INDUSTRY. THIS PROJECT IS FUNDED BY THE ADVANCED TECHNOLOGICAL EDUCATION PROGRAM THAT FOCUSES ON THE EDUCATION OF TECHNICIANS FOR THE ADVANCED-TECHNOLOGY FIELDS THAT DRIVE THE NATION'S ECONOMY. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

THE PUERTO RICO AGRICULTURAL EXTENSION SERVICE (PRAES) PROPOSED ACTIVITIES ARE BASED ON SIX CRITICAL ISSUES DEFINED IN THE 2021-2025 APPROVED POW. THESE INCLUDE: 1. FOOD SECURITY, PLANTS AND ANIMAL SYSTEMS; 2. EXTREME WEATHER, NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENT, AND SUSTAINABLE ENERGY; 3. FOOD SAFETY, SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY; 4. COMMUNITY, ECONOMY, AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT; 5. FAMILY AND WELL -BEING AND 6. POSITIVE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT. INTEGRATED EFFORTS AMONG EXTENSION AGENTS AND FAMILY EDUCATORS TO IMPROVE AGRI-BUSINESS ECONOMIC AND MARKETING STRATEGIES TO INCREASE FOOD SECURITY IN FARMS, HOMES, SCHOOLS, AND COMMUNITIES WILL CONTINUE. THE USE OF DRONES FOR ESTIMATION OF VEGETATION BIOMASS AND DEVELOPMENT OF WASTE MANAGEMENT PLANS ARE RECENT ADAPTED TOOLS BEING USE TO HELP FARMERS. TROUGH THE PLANT DISEASE CLINIC, EARLY DETECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF PESTS AND DISEASES CONTINUES TO BE CRITICAL FOR PLANT SYSTEMS. NEW DISEASES AND PESTS ARE MAINLY DISSEMINATED THROUGH SOCIAL MEDIA AND PRAES ONLINE WEB PAGES. CRITICAL ISSUE # 2 WILL BE ADDRESSED BY ENCOURAGING FARMERS TO INCREASE THE USE OF SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE PRACTICES THAT HELP IN PROTECTING OUR NATURAL RESOURCES SUCH AS COVER CROPS, NO-TILL AND ROTATIONAL GRAZING AND AID FARMERS, FAMILIES AND 4H MEMBERS TO PROMOTE THE USE OF RENEWABLE ENERGY. ADDITIONAL EFFORTS WILL IDENTIFY SUCCESSFUL ADAPTATIONS TO EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS BASED ON RISK EXPOSURE ASSESSMENTS, AGRICULTURAL BIODIVERSITY PRACTICES, BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES RELATED TO SOIL QUALITY AND, MITIGATION OF THREATS TO WATER QUALITY. IN TERMS OF CRITICAL ISSUE # 3, PRAES WILL CONTINUE OFFERING: THE FOOD SAFETY CERTIFICATION COURSE TO PEOPLE IN CHARGE OF RETAIL FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS, AND FORMAL EDUCATION TO PROFESSIONALS THAT ENFORCE FOOD COMPLIANCE REGULATIONS. RAES WILL ALSO CONTINUE OFFERING FOOD SAFETY COURSES SUCH AS THE FAMILIES BE FOOD SAFE WHICH IS ADAPTED TO MEET THE CLIENTELE'S NEEDS. ACTIVITIES RELATED TO CRITICAL ISSUE # 4 WILL FOSTER THE REGENERATION OF AGRICULTURE AND EMPLOYMENT. PROMOTING BETTER PAID EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES AND INCREASED LABOR EFFICIENCY ARE VITAL TO IMPROVE THE AVAILABILITY OF LABOR FOR FARM RECOVERY AND IMPROVING COMMUNITY CONDITIONS. ACTIVITIES ARE FOCUSED ON CAPACITY BUILDING IN AREAS OF COMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEMS, EMERGENCY PLANS, VOLUNTEER PROGRAMS, AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP. PRAES WILL CONTINUE COLLABORATING WITH THE CREATION OF ACTION PLANS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF ECONOMIC PROJECTS THAT GENERATE INCOME AND JOBS; AND WITH EDUCATION ACTIVITIES RELATED TO COMMUNITY SELF-MANAGEMENT, VOLUNTEERS' RESILIENCY, AND DEVELOPMENT OF EMERGENCY AND SECURITY PLANS FOR FAMILIES. IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF LIFE OF OUR VULNERABLE POPULATIONS WILL BE ADDRESSED THROUGH CRITICAL ISSUE # 5. THE HEALTH PROMOTION AND DISEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM TARGETS AREAS OF CHRONIC AND INFECTIOUS DISEASES AND PREVENTION INTERVENTIONS. THE FAMILY RESOURCE MANAGEMENT WILL FOCUS ON HELPING AND EMPOWERING THE INDIVIDUAL, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY TO FACE CURRENT AND FUTURE FINANCIAL NEEDS. EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS ON SPENDING AND SAVINGS PLANS AND ON MAKING STRATEGIC DECISIONS THAT FAVOR FAMILY WELL-BEING CONTINUE TO BE ONE OF OUR PILLARS. EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TARGETED THROUGH THE CRITICAL ISSUE # 5 WILL CREATE SAFE LEARNING SPACES, ESTABLISH POSITIVE CONTACTS, AND PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR CHILDREN AND YOUTH TO DEVELOP SKILLS THAT POSITIVELY CONTRIBUTE TO OUR SOCIETY. WE WILL CONTINUE WORKING WITH YOUTH LEADERS TO PROMOTE EMOTIONAL SUPPORT SYSTEMS FOR YOUTH VOLUNTEER LEADERS, AND EFFICIENT COPING MECHANISMS BEFORE, DURING AND AFTER NATURAL DISASTERS AND EMERGENCIES. OUR POW WILL PROMOTE EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES AT COMMUNITIES, SUPPORT YOUTH LEADERS, AND EXPAND 4-H ENRICHMENT ACTIVITIES TO HELP KIDS AND YOUTH MOVE FORWARD AFTER NATURAL DISASTERS AND EMERGENCIES.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR HAS BEEN UNDERGOING A PERIOD OF RAPID TRANSFORMATION, DRIVEN BY THE POWERFUL AND INTERCONNECTED IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE, DEMOGRAPHIC TRANSITIONS AND UNEVEN ECONOMIC GROWTH. ADVANCES IN IRRIGATION, FERTILIZATION, MECHANIZATION, AND BREEDING HAVE HELPED AGRICULTURE KEEP PACE WITH THE EXPLOSIVE GROWTH OF THE WORLD'S POPULATION, BUT AT ENORMOUS COSTS TO THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN HEALTH. CONVENTIONAL TECHNOLOGIES WILL NOT SOLVE THESE UBIQUITOUS CHALLENGES. EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES (ET) EMPLOYING DATA SCIENCE (DS), MACHINE LEARNING (ML) AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) HAS PROVIDED THE IMPETUS TO TRANSFORM THE OVERALL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEM AND LANDSCAPE AT MULTI-SCALE LEVELS. EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES (E.G. ROBOTICS, DRONES, SENSORS) SURROUNDING THE INTERNET OF THINGS (IOT) HAS PROPELLED AGRICULTURE EVEN FURTHER THROUGH INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGIES (ICTS) IN THE CYBER-PHYSICAL CYCLE OF FARM MANAGEMENT THIS WORK SEEKS TO STRENGTHEN CAPACITY AMONGST THE 1890INSTITUTIONS, CATALYZING OUR PARTICIPATION OF HOW ET SHAPES OUR FUTURE. THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE IN EMERGING INTERNET OF THINGS (E-IOT) TECHNOLOGIES BRINGS TOGETHER SCIENTISTS FROM (9) 1890 INSTITUTIONS -DSU, UMES, SU, TU, AAMU, SCSU, UAPB, NCA&T, AND FAMU WITH COLLABORATIVE SUPPORT FROM UC DAVIS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR NEXT- GENERATION FOOD SYSTEMS AND THE UNIVERSITY OF DELAWARE (UD) DATA SCIENCE INSTITUTE (DSI), ALL WITH A PROVEN RECORD OF EXCELLENCE IN AI AND DATA SCIENCE, AGRICULTURE, OUTREACH, AND EDUCATION. THE BROAD GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO ACHIEVE FOUNDATIONAL ADVANCES IN EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES TO ADDRESS PRESSING CHALLENGES IN AGRICULTURE. THE PROJECT WILL TACKLE FOUR (4) KEY AGRICULTURAL CHALLENGES: (1) THE DEVELOPMENT OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS WITH INCREASED AI, DS, ML CONTENT TO PRODUCE OUR NEXT GENERATION WORKFORCE; (2) RESEARCH AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT TRAINING TO INCREASE PARTICIPATION OF UNDERREPRESENTED AND DISADVANTAGED GROUPS; AND (3) EXTENSION TO SMALL AND MINORITY FARMERS IN THE DEMONSTRATION OF EMERGING TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS AND PROVIDING FEEDBACK ON THE INCENTIVES AND BARRIERS TO THEIR ADOPTION. THIS WORK WILL PROMOTE A NEXT GENERATION WORKFORCE AND ENABLE SMALL AND MINORITY FARMERS WITH THE KNOWLEDGE TO INCREASE FOOD PRODUCTION AND PROFITABILITY IN THE LONG TERM AS WELL AS IMPROVE RESILIENCY TO CLIMATE CHANGE.

awards.Description: ADDRESSING THE NEEDS OF STAKEHOLDERS IN AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND NUTRITION INDUSTRY IN OHIO AND US THROUGH EVANS ALLEN PROGRAM AT CENTRAL STATE UNIVERSITY CENTRAL STATE UNIVERSITY THROUGH ITS EVANS ALLEN RESEARCH PROGRAM EXPECTS TO FOCUS ON THE FOLLOWING THEMATIC RESEARCH AREAS IN AGRIC ULTURE, FOOD SCIENCES AND NUTRITION: AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY (AT) HAS NOT ALWAYS BEEN ECONOMICALLY VIABLE FOR SMALL OR MEDIUM FARM OPERATIONS. SMALL-SCALE AND SPECIALTY CROP GROWERS MAY NOT BENEFIT FROM THE WAVE OF TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCEMENTS AS LARGE-SCALE PRODUCTION GROWERS. INADEQUATE EFFORT HAS OCCURRED TO UPLIFT SMALL-SCALE FARMING TO MAKE AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY A PROFITABLE AND DESIRABLE CHOICE FOR BEGINNER FARMERS. THIS ISSUE NEEDS TO BE ADDRESSED FOR THE BETTERMENT OF THE SMALL SCALE, BEGINNING, SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED, AND SPECIALTY CROP GROWERS. SMALL-SCALE FARMERS WHO FARM LESS THAN 5 ACRES ARE CRITICAL FOR WORLD FOOD SECURITY AS THEY PRODUCE 35% OF THE WORLD'S FOOD. THEREFORE, THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS FOR SMALL-SCALE FARMING IS IMPERATIVE FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND WORLD FOOD SECURITY. CROSS DISCIPLINARY APPROACHES ARE NEEDED TO ADDRESS THIS CHALLENGE. APPLICATIONS OF MECHATRONICS THAT INTEGRATE EXPERTISE IN MECHANICAL ENGINEERING, ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING, COMPUTER CONTROL, MACHINE VISION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY IN A SEAMLESS MANNER IS GAINING TRACTION IN IMPROVING FOOD PRODUCTION. RESEARCH IN MECHANICAL DESIGN OF NEW OR MODIFYING AND ADAPTING EXISTING AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY FOR PRECISION DELIVERY OF NOVEL INTEGRATED AGRICULTURAL NUTRIENT AND PEST MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES, COORDINATED MACHINE CONTROL IN RESPONSE TO SENSORY FEEDBACK, SENSOR TECHNOLOGY AND HIGH-LEVEL PROGRAMMING ARE NEEDED TO IMPROVE EFFICIENCY OF FARMING SYSTEMS. PRECISION AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY IS A CRITICAL SOLUTION TO EXPAND THE ONGOING RESEARCH ON NON-CHEMICAL, HIGH ENER GY-BASED PEST CONTROL CONDUCTED BY RESEARCHERS IN CESTA WHICH REQUIRES ADDITIONAL CAPABILITIES IN MECHATRONICS ENGINEERING TO DEVELOP DEVICES THAT ENHANCE AGRICULTURAL EFFICIENCY, REDUCE COSTS AND IMPROVE SUSTAINABILITY. CSU ALSO INTENDS TO DEVELOP APPROPRIATE SERVICES FOR COMMERCIALIZING THE TECHNOLOGIES TO LOWER FARMING COSTS AND ENHANCE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT THROUGH HIGHER PAYING JOBS IN RELATED ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY COMPANIES. ALTERNATIVE CROPS ARE NEEDED TO PROVIDE GROWERS NEW REVENUE STREAMS. LARGE-SCALE ADOPTION OF ALTERNATIVE CROPS CAN REDUCE OVERPRODUCTION OF MAJOR CROPS, THEREBY INCREASING COMMODITY PRICES. IT IS RELEVANT TO EXPLORE AND DEVELOP KNOWLEDGE TO ESTABLISH VALUABLE NICHE MARKETS FOR ALTERNATIVE AND SPECIALTY CROPS. INTERESTING ALTERNATIVE CROPS FOR OHIO INCLUDE HEMP, HIGH-AMYLOSE CORN, PERENNIAL CROPS, MEDICINAL PLANTS, AND BIOMASS CROPS. HEMP CAN BE UTILIZED AS A FOOD, FIBER, FEED, BIOENERGY, AND MEDICINE. INCREASING OHIO HEMP PRODUCTION WILL DIVERSIFY THE STATE'S AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY, GIVE GROWERS ALTERNATIVE REVENUE STREAMS, REDUCE DEPENDENCE ON TWO CROP SYSTEMS (CORN-SOYBEANS), PROVIDE ECOLOGICAL SUSTAINABLE BENEFITS AND THAT ENHANCE HUMAN HEALTH. CENTRAL STATE IS CONDUCTING AGRONOMY AND PLANT BREEDING RESEARCH IN ALTERNATE, SPECIALTY AND MEDICINAL PLANTS UNDER CONVENTIONAL AND ORGANIC PRODUCTION SYSTEM. NEW HEMP VARIETIES BRED AND ADAPTED TO OHIO WILL PROVIDE GROWERS ACROSS THE REGION SUPERIOR GENETICS TO MAXIMIZE CROP YIELDS AND REDUCE CHANCES OF CROP FAILURE. THESE TRAITS WILL ENHANCE THE SUCCESS OF HEMP CROPS WITHIN THE REGION AND MAXIMIZE FARMER RETURNS. CSU WILL ALSO PURSUE DEVELOPING TECHNIQUES TO MAKE USE OF HEMP FIBER FOR COMPOSITE MATERIALS AND MEDICINAL PRODUCTS. A PROGRAM FOR THE IMPROVEMENT OF SPECIALTY CORN THAT WORKS WITH OHIO PRODUCERS TOWARD IDENTIFYING NEW MARKET OPPORTUNITIES BY THE DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIALIZATION OF HYBRID VARIETIES WITH USEFUL NOVEL STARCHES AS DETERMINED BY THE NEEDS OF THE END-USERS APPEARS NECESSARY. IN THIS REGARD HIGH-AMYLOSE CORN, WHICH HAS ELEVATED LEVELS OF AMYLOSE CONTENT IN THE STARCH HAS POTENTIAL BENEFITS. RECENT DEVELOPMENTS INDICATE ITS POTENTIAL UTILIZATION IN BIOPLASTICS AND BY FOOD COMPANIES FOR A STARCH TYPE THAT RESISTS DIGESTION. NATURAL PRODUCTS FROM HORTICULTURAL PRODUCTION THAT HAVE CAPACITY TO PROVIDE ENHANCED ECONOMIC VALUE TO AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS MAY ALSO BRING ECONOMIC BENEFITS TO OHIO PRODUCERS. THE POTENTIAL FOR NATURAL PRODUCTS TO REMEDIATE SOME OF THE MOST CURRENT PUBLIC CONCERNS SUCH AS HUMAN HEALTH AND NUTRITION, PESTS, AND PATHOGENS, AS WELL AS OTHER SOCIETAL PROBLEMS MERITS EXPLORATION. CENTRAL STATE IS ENGAGED IN DEVELOPING NATURAL PRODUCTS FROM PLANTS TO ESTABLISH VALUABLE NICHE MARKETS FOR ALTERNATIVE AND SPECIALTY CROPS. SOIL SECURITY IS A CRITICAL COMPONENT OF PLANT PRODUCTIVITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY IN AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS. INFORMED MANAGEMENT OF SOIL RESOURCES IS IMPERATIVE TO EFFECTIVELY MANAGE NATURAL RESOURCES.,. AN ASSESSMENT OF SOIL INFORMATION AND HEALTH AT LOCAL, REGIONAL, AND GLOBAL SCALES WILL PROVIDE A HOLISTIC SYSTEM-BASED APPROACH TO ADDRESS THE ISSUES AT THE NEXUS OF PLANT, ANIMAL, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SYSTEMS. CENTRAL STATE RESEARCHERS WILL USE ADVANCED TECHNIQUES AND INSTRUMENTATION THAT HARNESSES THE RECENT DEVELOPMENTS IN AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES INCLUDING, PROXIMAL SENSING, SATELLITE SENSING, DRONE-BASED SENSING, SOIL MICROBIOLOGY, ISOTOPE GEOCHEMISTRY, AND PESTICIDE CHEMISTRY TO SOLVE BROAD SOCIETAL NEEDS SUCH AS CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION, CARBON MARKETS, RENEWABLE ENERGY SYSTEMS, NON- POINT SOURCE POLLUTION ABATEMENT, ENHANCED CROP PRODUCTIVITY, DIVERSIFIED CROPPING SYSTEMS AND POLLINATOR BEHAVIOR AND HEALTH. RESEARCHERS WILL ASSESS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF SEVERAL AGRICULTURAL BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES IN REDUCING NUTRIENT LOADS IN THE GREAT AND LITTLE MIAMI WATERSHEDS THAT DRAIN INTO THE OHIO RIVER AND SUBSEQUENTLY INTO THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER AND GULF OF MEXICO. CENTRAL STATE EXPECTS TO ACHIEVE THIS BY UTILIZING ADVANCE GEOSPATIAL AND AI TECHNOLOGIES, MODELING AND OTHER INNOVATIVE LAB AND FIELD TECHNIQUES COUPLED WITH ON FARM RESEARCH. WATER ISSUES IN THE US ARE RELATED TO 1) VARIABILITY IN AVAILABILITY OF THE RESOURCE FOR AGRICULTURE, DOMESTIC INDUSTRIAL AND COMMERCIAL USES, FIREFIGHTING, AND RECREATION; 2) FLOODS AND DROUGHTS; 3) WATER QUALITY IN AGRICULTURAL AND URBAN AREAS; 4) ECONOMICS OF WATER RESOURCES AND 5) WAYS FOR ENERGY GENERATION. THE MAJOR PHENOMENON OF CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS ALL ASPECTS OF WATER, WHICH REQUIRES PLANNING STRUCTURAL AND NON-STRUCTURAL MITIGATION MEASURES. A MAJOR WATER ISSUE IN OHIO IS RELATED TO WATER QUALITY. NITROGEN AND PHOSPHORUS IN AGRICULTURAL RUNOFF AND LEACHING CONTINUES TO BE A NON-POINT SOURCE POLLUTION AFFECTING WATER QUALITY IN OHIO WATERSHEDS BY CAUSING HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS. TO DATE, MINIMAL RESEARCH HAS BEEN DONE IN CROPPED ACRES OF SOUTHWESTERN OHIO TO QUANTIFY THE IMPACT OF NUTRIENT POLLUTION ON WATER QUALITY. CENTRAL STATE RESEARCHERS WILL ADDRESS WATER QUALITY ISSUES IN SOUTHWESTERN OHIO BY TARGETED IMPLEMENTATIONOF AGRICULTURAL BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. IN URBAN LANDSCAPES, A WATER QUALITY ISSUE AFFECTING MUNICIPAL STAKEHOLDERS IS MANAGING THE WATER AND WASTEWATER SYSTEMS UNDER THEIR RESPECTIVE JURISDICTIONS. THE WASTEWATERS FROM THESE SYSTEMS, THOUGH TREATED AND RELEASED STILL CARRY CONSIDERABLE LOADS OF NON-POINT SOURCE POLLUTION. MAJOR WORK ELEMENTS INVOLVE DEVELOPING GUIDELINES FOR WATERSHED LEVEL DECISION MAKING ON WATER QUALITY RESTORATION AND IMPROVEMENTS BY THE MUNICIPALITIES AND COUNTIES; ENHANCE ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY; EXPANSION OF MODELING AS A DECISION-MAKING TOOL TO INCLUDE SOCIOECONOMIC FACTORS; ENHANCING THE SMART MODELS TO INCLUDE OTHER AND EMERGING "CONTAMINANTS OF CONCERN" AND AUGMENTING WASTEWATER SMART SENSORS WITH BIOSENSORS TO DETECT VIRUSES LEADING TO COUNTY-WIDE PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS. CENTRAL STATE RESEARCHERS WILL CONDUCT RESEARCH ON THESE WORK ELEMENTS. POLLINATOR HEALTH IS CRUCIAL FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE INTO THE FUTURE. HONEYBEES ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT MANAGED POLLINATORS CONTR IBUTING $15 BILLION FOR THE U.S. ECONOMY, BUT THE HONEYBEE COLONIES ARE IN A 40-50% DECLINE IN THE COUNTRY. MANAGED BEE COLONIES ARE IN A 60% ANNUAL DECLINE IN OHIO. PROMOTING MITE RESISTANT BEES IS ONE OF THE MOST EFFECTIVE WAYS TO MITIGATE THE BEE DECLINE. IT IS IMPERATIVE THAT TO DEVELOP NEW METHODS FOR INCREASING GENETIC DIVERSITY AND TO IMPROVE QUEEN BEE QUALITY. THE LIMITING FACTORS AFFECTING LOCAL HONEYBEE RESOURCES INCLUDE FEWER QUEENS AND THE NUCLEI AVAILABLE TO FULFILL THE DEMAND OF BEEKEEPERS IN THE REGION. CENTRAL STATE UNIVERSITY EXPECTS TO GROW THE BEE GENOMIC PROGRAM TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF THE OHIO STAKEHOLDERS INVOLVED IN POLLINATOR MANAGEMENT. HUMAN HEALTH ENCOMPASSES MANY FACTORS: BEHAVIORAL, ECONOMIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, CULTURAL, EDUCATIONAL, AND GENETIC. DIET AND NUTRITION A RE IMPORTANT TO OVERALL HEALTH. DISEASES RELATED TO OBESITY, SEDENTARY LIFESTYLES, NUTRIENT DEFICIENCIES AND FOOD INSECURITY, ARE MAJOR DIETARY HEALTH CONCERNS IN THE U.S AND IN OHIO. CENTRAL STATE EXPECT TO DEVELOP METHODS THAT ARE NEEDED TO POSITIVELY IMPACT COMMUNITY HEALTH, BY WORKING WITH INDIVIDUALS AND SYSTEMS TO DETERMINE THE BEST PRACTICES IN HEALTH PROMOTION. UNIVERSITY RESEARCHERS WILL CONDUCT STUDIES ON FACTORS RELATED TO HEART HEALTH OF AFRICAN AMERICAN POPULATION TO FIND PATHWAYS TO IMPROVE WELLNESS OF THE AFFECTED COMMUNITIES. THROUGH RESEARCH, WE ALSO EXPECT TO FOCUS ON IDENTIFYING PREVENTATIVE MECHANISMS FOR REDUCING ANGINA AND DETERMINING THE EFFECTS OF GASOTRANSMITTERS SUCH AS NITRIC OXIDE (NO) AND HYDROGEN SULFIDE (H2S) IN DIABETES AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE MODELS INCLUDING TISSUE CULTURE, TO GUIDE POSSIBLE INTERVENTION MECHANISMS USING NUTRITIONAL APPROACHES. STUDIES IN THESE DISEASE MODELS WILL PROVIDE VALUABLE INFORMATION FOR IMPROVING HUMAN HEALTH AND ASSOCIATED SCIENCE. FOOD SAFETY AUGMENTS HUMAN HEALTH. FRESH PRODUCE CONSUMPTION HAS INCREASED IN THE US BECAUSE OF INCREASING HEALTH CONSCIOUSNESS OF C ONSUMERS, IMPROVED YEAR-ROUNDAVAILABILITY, CREATIVE MARKETING, AND IMPROVED VARIETIES. FRESH PRODUCE CONSUMPTION INCREASE HOWEVER, HAS COINCIDED WITH SEVERAL FOODBORNE PATHOGENIC CASES OUTBREAKS AND DISEASES LINKED TO PRODUCE WHICH ARE MAJOR THREATS TO FOOD INDUSTRY. FOR THE PAST FEW YEARS, MOST FOODBORNE CONTAMINATION AND OUTBREAKS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH FRESH PRODUCE (FRUIT AND VEGETABLES). HUMAN PATHOGENIC BACTERIA, SALMONELLA, LISTERIA, AND ESCHERICHIA COLI O157:H7, STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS, AND SHIGELLA, AND NOROVIRUS, HEPATITIS A VIRUS, AND PROTOZOA ARE THE LEADING CONTAMINANTS IN PRODUCE INDUSTRY. CURRENTLY, THERE IS LIMITED LITERATURE IN UNDERSTANDING THE HUMAN PATHOGEN SOURCES, SURVIVAL BEHAVIOR IN PRODUCE AND ENVIRONMENT, AND MODE OF TRANSMISSION AND CONTAMINATION DURING PRODUCTION. EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE AND CHANGES IN GLOBAL TRADE AND CONSUMPTION PATTERNS ARE EXPECTED TO INFLUENCE THE QUALITY OF FRESH PRODUCE AND IMPACTS FOOD SAFETY. CLIMATE CHANGE EFFECTS INCLUDING EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS AND NATURAL DISASTERS, SUCH AS FLOODS AND DROUGHT HAVE INCREASED THE FREQUENCY OF HEAVY RAINS, FREQUENT AND LONGER DROUGHT PERIODS, ACIDIFICATION OF WATER, CO2 ENRICHED ATMOSPHERE, AND EXTREME PRECIPITATIONS WITH ALTERED PATTERNS AND POTENTIAL RISING IN SEA LEVELS. ALL THESE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ARE EXPECTED TO IMPACT THE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION METHODS AND POTENTIALLY SUPPORT THE GROWTH, SURVIVAL, ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE, AND EMERGENT OF NEW STRAINS OF PATHOGENIC MICROORGANISMS ASSOCIATE WITH FOOD AND WATER SOURCES. ALSO, THE INSECT PESTS, MICROBIAL VECTORS, POPULATION IS EXPECTED TO GROW DUE TO ALTERED WEATHER PATTERNS. INCREMENT IN TEMPERATURES IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE THE RISE OF SEA LEVEL THAT MAY INFLUENCE HUMAN PATHOGENS SURVIVAL AND PROLIFERATION IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. CENTRAL STATE UNIVERSITY INTENDS TO DEVELOP OF A FOOD SAFETY RESEARCH PROGRAM TO ADDRESS THE FOOD SECURITY ISSUES IN OHIO. WORKFORCE DIVERSITY IN AGRICULTURE, FOOD, AND NUTRITION INDUSTRY IS A CRITICAL NEED AT THE STATE AND NATIONAL LEVEL. CENTRAL STATE AS ONE OF THE 19 HBCU LAND GRANT INSTITUTIONS IN THE COUNTRY IS DEDICATED TO SERVING THE UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURE, FOOD, AND NUTRITION DISCIPLINES. THE UNIVERSITY WILL ENGAGE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES IN THE ABOVE DISCUSSED THEMATIC RESEARCH AREAS AS UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH ASSISTANTS IN THE LAB AND IN THE FIELD. THE STUDENTS WILL BE PROVIDED OPPORTUNITIES FOR PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT IN USDA DISCIPLINES TO FOSTER A DIVERSIFIED WORKFORCE.

awards.Description: THROUGH THE INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH, THE GOAL OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AT TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY IS TO CREATE AND COMMUNICATE NEW KNOWLEDGE IN THE AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES. THROUGH OUR INNOVATIVE RESEARCH, WE ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF HUMANKIND, FOCUSING ON FINDING SOLUTIONS TO CHALLENGES FACED BY SOCIALLY AND ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED GROUPS, AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROSPERITY OF THE CITIZENS OF TENNESSEE, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. RESEARCH IN TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURE IS ORGANIZED TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL ISSUES DESCRIBED BELOW. ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY SAFEGUARDING AND ENHANCING THE NATURAL RESOURCE ENVIRONMENT HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY COMPLEX WITHIN ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, RESOURCE AND PERSONAL CONTEXTS. THROUGH COLLABORATION AMONG RESEARCHERS, INDUSTRY, PRODUCERS, ENVIRONMENTAL GROUPS, AND GOVERNMENT, WE ARE HELPING PRESERVE A DIVERSE AND RESILIENT ENVIRONMENT FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY HELPING FARMS AND AGRICULTURE BUSINESSES BECOME MORE PROFITABLE AND INDIVIDUALS BECOME FINANCIALLY SECURE BOOSTS THE LOCAL, STATE, AND NATIONAL ECONOMIES. OUR PROGRAMS STRIVE TO STRENGTHEN THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF ALL FACETS OF AGRIBUSINESS, AND IMPROVE THE FINANCIAL LITERACY OF TENNESSEANS AND BEYOND SO THEY MAY BUILD AND PROTECT WEALTH FOR THEMSELVES AND FUTURE GENERATIONS. STRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH MAKING HEALTHY CHOICES IS IMPORTANT FOR HUMANS, ANIMALS, AND EVEN OUR PLANET. AS A LEADER IN NUTRITION, ANIMAL WELFARE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, WE ARE WORKING TO UNDERSTAND HOW FOOD, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND SOCIAL CONNECTIONS AFFECT OVERALL HEALTH. FROM FOOD SAFETY TO DISEASE PREVENTION AND MAINTENANCE TO THE STATE OF OUR ENVIRONMENT, THESE EFFORTS WILL HELP AMERICANS AND THE REST OF THE WORLD LEAD HEALTHIER LIVES FOR GENERATIONS TO COME. SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS SAFE, SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS THAT ARE SOCIALLY, ECONOMICALLY, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY RESPONSIBLE ARE KEY TO ENHANCING THE LIVES OF TENNESSEANS AND SUPPORTING A GROWING GLOBAL POPULATION. WE ARE EXPLORING WAYS TO DELIVER DISCOVERIES USING A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO AGRICULTURE PRODUCTIVITY THAT WILL PROVIDE CUSTOMIZABLE SOLUTIONS FOR PRODUCERS. UTILIZING FACULTY IN THE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SCIENCES, OUR RESE ARCH ADDRESSES THESE CRITICAL ISSUES THROUGH FACULTY GROUPS IN THE PLANT, ANIMAL, FOOD, AND HUMAN SCIENCES. THESE FACULTY-LED GROUPS FACILITATE THE IDENTIFICATION OF RESEARCH PRIORITIES WITHIN OUR CRITICAL ISSUES THAT ARE OF IMPORTANCE TO STAKEHOLDER GROUPS. WE CONDUCT RESEARCH IN AGRICULTURAL LEADERSHIP, EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION THAT BRIDGES THE GAP BETWEEN THE GENERAL PUBLIC AND SCIE NTISTS WORKING TO SOLVE CURRENT AND EMERGING CHALLENGES RELATED TO SUSTAINABLY FEEDING AN EVER-GROWING POPULATION UNDER VARIOUS ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIETAL COMPLICATIONS. THIS RESEARCH ALSO BUILDS HUMAN AND INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITYNEEDED BY A VARIETY OF PUBLIC, PRIVATE, AND NONPROFIT EMPLOYERS IN THE AGRICULTURE SECTOR. ALSO STUDIED ARE WAYS TO DEVELOP HUMAN CAPACITY AND PROVIDE LEADERSHIP WITHIN COMMUNITIES. MUCH RESEARCH IN THIS AREA ALSO IDENTIFIES THE IMPACT OF TECHNOLOGY IN AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION, TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS LECTURE-CAPTURE, DRONES, ROBOTS, EXTENDED REALITY, AND 360-DEGREE VIDEO. IN THE AREA OF AGRIBUSINESS, WE HAVE STRONG APPLIED-RESEARCH COMPONENT. WE PREPARE STUDENTS, FARMERS, AND STAKEHOLDERS IN THE USE OF ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MANAGEMENT COMPETENCIES TO TAKE ON THE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES OF A DYNAMIC AGRI-FOOD SYSTEM. THE RESEARCH AREA EMPHASIZES PROMOTING, DEVELOPING, AND IMPROVING THE UTILIZATION OF RESEARCH, OUTREACH CAPABILITIES AND OPPORTUNITIES INVOLVING AGRIBUSINESSES, NATURAL RESOURCES AND COMMUNITIES. MAIN ACTIVITIES INCLUDE INVESTIGATIONS ON THE SOLE OR COMBINATION OF STRATEGIES FOR PROFITABILITY, AND THE SUSTAINABILITY, SURVIVAL, EFFICIENCY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF AGRICULTURALOPERATIONS, PARTICULARLY SMALL FARM OPERATIONS. ANTICIPATED RESULTS INCLUDE FARMERS' ADOPTION OF NEW CROPS; INVESTMENT FOR ALTERNATE INCOME DIVERSIFICATION STRATEGIES SUCH AS AGRITOURISM; ENHANCED KNOWLEDGE ON BENEFITS AND COSTS OF SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES; IMPROVED FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AND MARKETING STRATEGIES AND DEVELOPMENT OF ENTREPRENEURSHIP SKILLS. RESEARCH IN ANIMAL SCIENCE IS DIRECTED AT IMPROVING LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SYSTEMS BY GENERATING NOVEL FINDINGS THAT IMPACT ANIMAL WELL-BEING AND PERFORMANCE. SUB-DISCIPLINES SUCH AS GENETICS, HEALTH, NUTRITION, AND REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY ARE INTEGRATED IN THE POULTRY AND RUMINANT LIVESTOCK RESEARCH ENDEAVORS. RESEARCH SPANS FROM BASIC, MOLECULAR MODELS TO APPLIED, WHOLE-ANIMAL SYSTEMS. PRIMARY END-USERS OF THE RESEARCH FINDINGS ARE LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS THAT ARE OFTEN SOCIALLY-DISADVANTAGED, RESOURCE-LIMITED OWNER-OPERATORS OF SMALL-SCALE ENTERPRISES. WE HAVE RESEARCH EFFORTS DIRECTED AT ELUCIDATING, MOLECULARLY AND FUNCTIONALLY, ANIMAL IMMUNE AND METABOLIC GENES. IN PARTICULAR, THOSE GENES THAT HAVE ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITIES AND THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL. WE ARE USING COMBINED APPROACHES OF BIOINFORMATICS, GENETICS AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY TO ELUCIDATE GENES OR GENE FAMILIES THAT ARE POTENTIALLY IMPORTANT IN ANIMAL HEALTH. SOME OF OUR ANIMAL PRODUCTION RESEARCH EMPHASIZES GOAT PRODUCTION. PROJECTS HAVE FOCUSED ON EVALUATING BREEDS TO GENERATE RECOMMENDATIONS ON HOW TO BEST USE THE DIFFERENT BREEDS FOR ENHANCED COMMERCIAL MEAT GOAT PRODUCTION. PRODUCERS HAVE MODIFIED THEIR GENETIC MANAGEMENT DECISION-MAKING LEADING TO IMPROVED HERD HEALTH, PERFORMANCE, AND ECONOMIC RETURN. IN POULTRY RESEARCH, THE CURRENT DEMAND FOR POULTRY AND POULTRY PRODUCTS REQUIRES A GAIN IN GENETIC POTENTIAL COMPLEMENTED WITH NUTRITIONAL REGIMENS THAT MAXIMIZE GROWTH AND IMPROVE EFFICIENCY OF FEED UTILIZATION. EXAMINATION OF OPTIMAL FEED COMPOSITION AND ALLOCATION IS OPTIMIZING SPECIFIC AMINO ACID CONCENTRATIONS. FEEDING THESE NEW LEVELS OF AMINO ACIDS WILLREDUCE FEEDING COST IN GUINEA FOWL PRODUCTION. OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE PREVENTION IS ADDRESSED IN A PROGRAM THAT FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING A SMARTPHONE APPLICATION FOR WIC FAMILIES THAT WILL PROVIDE TOOLS TO MAKE USING THEIR BENEFITS EASIER WHILE PROVIDING HEALTHY RECIPES, NUTRITION EDUCATION, AND A GOAL TRACKING TOOL. HEALTHY EATING EXTENDS BEYOND LIMITING INTAKE OF FATS AND CALORIES. OUR NUTRITION RESEARCH IS AIMED AT UNDERSTANDING THE EFFECTS AND MECHANISMS OF FOOD-DERIVED BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS AND THEIR ROLE IN COMBATING HUMAN CHRONIC DISEASES SUCH CANCER, OBESITY, AND DIABETES. RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE DIRECT EVIDENCE THAT HUMAN CHRONIC DISEASE CAN BE PREVENTED OR TREATED BY SELECTING FOODS HAVING HIGH LEVELS OF BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS. FOOD IS A CORNERSTONE OF HUMAN EXISTENCE. ONGOING FOOD SCIENCE RESEARCH FOCUSES ON IMPROVING THE SAFETY, QUALITY, SHELF-LIFE, NUTRIENT PROFILE AND SENSORY ATTRIBUTES OF NOVEL FOOD INGREDIENTS, DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING ADVANCED AND INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES FOR FOOD PROCESSING, MANUFACTURING, PACKAGING, AND SANITATION TO EFFECTIVELY REDUCE THE PRESENCE OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS. ALSO, WE ARE DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING NOVEL STRATEGIES FOR THE EFFECTIVE CONTROL OF PERSISTENT RESERVOIRS OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS AND MITIGATING ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE ACROSS THE FOOD CHAIN. FOR EXAMPLE, WE ARE LOOKING AT NEW WAYS TO REMOVE PATHOGENS FROM FOODS BY PRECISELY DEFINING THE LIMITS OF USING UV LIGHT AS A SUBSTITUTE FOR PASTEURIZATION TO ACHIEVE A SPECIFIED LETHALITY FOR DEADLY AGENTS IN FOODS. THIS PROCESS IS USING ADVANCED MATHEMATICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELS. TECHNIQUES DEVELOPED IN THIS PROGRAM ARE ALSO BEING INVESTIGATED FOR POSSIBLE APPLICATION TO CONTROL THE SPREAD OF SARS-COV-2 AND OTHER VIRUSES. OTHER FOOD SCIENCE RESEARCH IS ADDRESSING THE PROBLEM OF CAMPYLOBACTER. THIS ORGANISM IS ONE OF THE MOST COMMON CAUSES OF DIARRHEAL ILLNESS IN THE UNITED STATES. DUE TO THE PREVALENCE OF CAMPYLOBACTER IN RAW CHICKEN PRODUCTS, ROUTINE AND RELIABLE MONITORING IS NECESSARY TO REDUCE ITS IMPACT UPON HUMAN HEALTH. THE METHOD BEING DEVELOPED IS INTENDED TO BE USED BY FOOD INDUSTRY AND REGULATORY TESTING LABORATORIES TO FACILITATE IMPROVED IDENTIFICATION OF CAMPYLOBACTER IN PROCESSING FACILITIES AND FINAL PRODUCTS. TO MITIGATE THE SPREAD OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANT CONTAMINANTS IN FOODS, WE HAVE RESEARCH THAT HAS GENERATED A SERIES OF HOTSPOT MAPS THAT WILL BE USED IN WORKSHOPS/WEBINARS TO ILLUSTRATE ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANT BACTERIAL COMMUNITIES ON PRODUCER'S FARMS. BY USING PERSONALIZED HOTSPOT MAPS THAT DISPLAY THE FREQUENCY OF ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANT BACTERIA IN FARMS, PRODUCERS WILL MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ON THE USAGE OF ANTIBIOTICS IN THEIR LIVESTOCK, THUS REDUCING THE THREAT OF CONTAMINATION OF FOOD CROPS FERTILIZED WITH THE ANTIMICROBIAL-RESISTANT MANURE. RESEARCH IN NATURAL RESOURCES USES MULTIDISCIPLINE APPROACHES TO UNDERSTAND AND ATTENUATE PROBLEMS CAUSED BY CLIMATE CHANGE, LAND DE GRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, EMERGING CONTAMINANTS, AND ANTHROPOGENIC STRESSORS. TRADITIONAL AND CUTTING-EDGE CHEMISTRY METHODS ARE USED TO STUDY FATE OF CHEMICALS IN THE ENVIRONMENT, THE INTERACTION OF HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES WITH SOILS AND WATER AND BIOGEOCHEMICAL CYCLES. BIOTECHNOLOGY IS USED TO STUDY AND RECTIFY HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS, WILDLIFE DISEASES AND PARASITES, MONITOR RARE AND ENDANGERED SPECIES, AND SOIL HEALTH. GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS, REMOTE SENSING AND ADVANCED STATISTICS ARE USED TO MODEL CLIMATE CHANGE ON A LARGE SCALE, WILDLIFE ECOSYSTEMS, DETERMINE THE VALUE OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND DOCUMENT WATER RESOURCES. OUR RESEARCH TAKES PLACE IN CHEMISTRY LABS, COMPUTER LABS, RURAL AND URBAN SETTINGS AS WE SEEK TO SUSTAIN AND IMPROVE THE NATION'S NATURAL RESOURCES. IN ADDITION TO RESEARCH, WE BUILD INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY AND STRENGTHEN OUR ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAM THROUGH BRIDGE PROGRAMS, STUDENT RECRUITMENT AND MENTORING, STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS, AGGRESSIVE PROPOSAL WRITING AND CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT. THE GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A STRONG DIVERSE WORKFORCE IN THE NATURAL RESOURCES THAT REFLECTS OUR NATION'S DEMOGRAPHICS. PLANT SCIENCE RESEARCH INCLUDES DIVERSE FIELDS IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS WITH A FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND APPLYING SCIENTIFIC AND BIOTECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES TO IMPROVE CROP PRODUCTIVITY, REDUCE LOSSES FROM DISEASE, INSECT PESTS, AND TOXIC METAL STRESS; IN ADDITION TO IMPROVING THE UNDERSTANDING OF PLANT STRESS TOLERANCE MECHANISMS FOR HANDLING HEAT, DROUGHT AND OTHER STRESS FACTORS. RESEARCH INCLUDES THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR IMPROVING THE PRODUCTION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT OF ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS FOR REDUCING PESTICIDE INPUTS IN CROP PRODUCTION SYSTEMS SUCH AS MICROBIAL-BASED PRODUCTS, PHEROMONES, AND PLANT OILS, PLANT GENETIC RESISTANCE AND BY BROADENING SOYBEAN GENETIC DIVERSITY FOR FUTURE GAINS IN CROP PRODUCTIVITY AND PREPAREDNESS FOR EMERGING NEW DISEASES AND INSECT PESTS. CROPS ADDRESSED ARE DIVERSE, INCLUDING VEGETABLES, CORN, SOYBEANS, ORNAMENTAL NURSERY CROPS, BIOENERGY CROPS, HYDROPONICS, AND URBAN AGRICULTURE. TECHNOLOGICAL CONTRIBUTIONS FROM THIS RESEARCH INCLUDE INCREASING CROP DIVERSITY BY INTRODUCING NEW EXOTIC VEGETABLES AND AMARANTH, DEVELOPING NEW CROP ALTERNATIVES LIKE HEMP, AND BIOFUEL ALTERNATIVES SUCH AS PERENNIAL SWITCHGRASS AND WINTER CANOLA THAT HAVE IMPROVED DIGESTIBILITY AND PROCESSING, AND DEVELOPING NEW PLANTS TOLERANT TO HEAT STRESS. OTHER RESEARCH ACTIVITIES ON BEST CROP MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, NITROGEN APPLICATION RATES TO ENHANCE YIELD AND FEEDSTOCK CHARACTERISTICS, THE BEST WINTER CANOLA VARIETIES AND NITROGEN RATES FOR TENNESSEE DELIVER SERVICES OF VALUE TO SOCIETY. AN OVERALL LACK OF CROP DIVERSITY IN THE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS OF THE SOUTHEASTERN UNITED STATES INCREASES THE THREATS OF DISEASE EPIDEMICS, INSECT PEST OUTBREAKS OR RISKS OF CROP FAILURE DUE TO ABIOTIC STRESSES. IT IS IMPORTANT TO DEVELOP ALTERNATIVE CROPS FOR PRODUCTIVE SYSTEMS. RESEARCH TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE HAS PRODUCED THE RELEASE OF TWO GRAIN AMARANTH VARIETIES AND THE RELEASE OF TWO GRAIN LEGUME VARIETIES. THESE ALTERNATIVE CROPS GIVE PRODUCERS OPTIONS IN SELECTING PRODUCTION MARKETS. ANOTHER PROGRAM LEADING TO CROP DIVERSITY IS EXAMINING THE ROLE OF SWEET SORGHUM AS A POTENTIAL DEDICATED US BIOFUEL CROP. THIS PROGRAM IS ESTABLISHING INNOVATIVE PROTOCOLS FOR SWEET SORGHUM GENETIC ENHANCEMENT. AS MORE KNOWLEDGE IS GAINED ABOUT THE INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF HUMAN IMPACTS ON THE EARTH, THE ROLE OF ANTIBIOTIC CONTAMINATION ON SOIL HEALTH IS BEING EXAMINED. MICRONUTRIENT DEFICIENCY IS A MAJOR CONCERN IN THE PRODUCTION OF SOME CROPS, SOME OF OUR RESEARCH WILL SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE THE UNDERSTANDING THE BIOGEOCHEMICAL CYCLING OF MICRONUTRIENTS IN THE PRESENCE OF ANTIBIOTICS. THREATS FROM DISEASE AND INSECT PESTS ARE BEING ADDRESSED IN A NUMBER OF RESEARCH PROGRAMS. PLANT DISEASE IS A MAJOR THREAT TO GLOBAL FOOD PRODUCTION COSTING THE US ECONOMY AN ESTIMATED $33 BILLION ANNUALLY IN YIELD LOSS. WE HAVE RESEARCH THAT IS FOCUSED ON UNEARTHING THE MOLECULAR SECRETS OF PLANT-BACTERIAL INTERACTIONS THAT RESULT IN TWO IMPORTANT DISEASES OF VEGETABLES - BACTERIAL SOFT ROT OF ALL VEGETABLES AND BACTERIAL WILT OF CUCURBITS CROPS. RESEARCH HAS IDENTIFIED ACCESSIONS RESISTANT TO WILT DISEASE AND WHICH CAN BE EMPLOYED IN A BREEDING PROGRAM FOR RESISTANCE CULTIVARS. OTHER DISEASE RESEARCH IS EXAMINING THE USE OF BIOCONTROL AGENTS FOR DISEASE MANAGEMENT. THESE ALTERNATIVES TO CHEMICAL FUNGICIDES WILL PROVIDE TOOLS FOR DISEASE MANAGEMENT IN VEGETABLE PRODUCTION ESPECIALLY IN ORGANIC FARMING AND REDUCE USAGE OF TOXIC CHEMICALS IN CONVENTIONAL FARMING. IPM IS A CROP PROTECTION PRACTICE THAT IS COST EFFECTIVE, ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND AND SOCIALLY ACCEPTABLE. TO FULFILL THIS NEED, WE CONDUCT RESEARCH FOCUSED ON CONDUCTING APPLIED RESEARCH EXPERIMENTS AND EDUCATING STAKEHOLDERS ON IPM THROUGH TRAINING AND PUBLICATIONS. IN-SERVICE TRAINING PROGRAMS FOR EXTENSION AGENTS AND IPM WORKSHOPS FOR OTHER STAKEHOLDERS ARE CONDUCTED ON STATE-WIDE BASIS IN EAST, MIDDLE AND WEST TENNESSEE REGIONS. INVASIVE INSECTS ARE A MAJOR CONCERN IN NURSERY PRODUCTION. OUR RESEARCH IS PRODUCING DATA FOR NEW PESTICIDE REGULATIONS FOR FIRE ANT, JAPANESE BEETLE AND OTHER IMPORTANT INSECTS THAT ARE REDUCING WORKER EXPOSURE RISK, SAVING PRODUCERS TIME, AND OVERALL REDUCING THE COST OF PRODUCTION. MORE PRODUCER SAVINGS ARE EXPECTED WITH NEW PROTOCOLS UNDER DEVELOPMENT. SUSTAINABILITY RESEARCH WILL LEAD TO NEW PRACTICES THAT RESULTS IN REDUCTION OF INPUTS (PESTICIDES, FERTILIZER, WATER, LABOR, ETC.) IN THE NURSERY PRODUCTION SYSTEM, THUS ENHANCING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE INDUSTRY, IMPROVING OUR ENVIRONMENT, REDUCING PRODUCTION COSTS FOR GROWERS, IMPROVING CROP QUALITY, AND BROADENING THE MARKET FOR TENNESSEE GREEN INDUSTRY PRODUCTS. TO ADDRESS THE WELL-BEING AND HEALTH OF INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH IN FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES IS FOCUSED ON IMPROVING THE LIVES OF OUR STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH FCS EDUCATION, LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNICATION TO IMPROVE NOT ONLY THEIR HEALTH AND W ELL-BEING, BUT ALSO THEIR RELATIONSHIPS AND RESOURCES. THIS GROUP IS CONTINUING TO FOCUS ON EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS, LIVING WITH CHRONIC DISEASES, FOOD SECURITY VIA FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND OF COURSE, MITIGATING THE EFFECTS OF COVID-19 AS WE LIVE THROUGH THE P ANDEMIC. awards.Description: SINCE 1882, THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE AGRESEARCH (FORMERLY THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION) HAS SERVED AS THE BACKBONE OF TENNESSEE'S AGRI-FORESTRY ECONOMY THROUGH RESEARCH, INNOVATION, AND APPLICATION. AS THE STATE'S TOP INDUSTRY, AGRI-FORESTRY CONTRIBUTES $103 BILLION ANNUALLY TO TENNESSEE'S ECONOMY. WORKING IN TANDEM WITH UT EXTENSION, MORE THAN 850 AGRESEARCH FACULTY, STAFF, AND GRADUATE STUDENTS ADDRESS CHALLENGES FACING AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES THROUGH SOLUTION-ORIENTED RESEARCH AND DISSEMINATION OF KNOWLEDGE TO FARMERS, ALLIED INDUSTRIES, AND CONSUMERS. UT AGRESEARCH OPERATES TEN RESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS (RECS) ACROSS TENNESSEE, COVERING DIVERSE GEOGRAPHIES, PRODUCTION SYSTEMS, CROPS, AND LIVESTOCK. THESE 40,000 ACRES OF FIELD LABORATORIES ALLOW RESEARCHERS TO CONDUCT TRIALS UNDER REAL WORLD CONDITIONS AND SERVE AS PLATFORMS FOR OUTREACH THROUGH ROUGHLY 20 FIELD DAYS EACH YEAR, ATTRACTING TENS OF THOUSANDS OF PARTICIPANTS FROM ACROSS THE STATE, REGION, AND BEYOND. THE RECS ALSO PROVIDE HANDS-ON LEARNING FOR COLLEGE STUDENTS AND YOUTH. AGRESEARCH ENCOMPASSES SEVEN ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS AND ONE SCHOOL OF NATURAL RESOURCES, WITH ABOUT 150 FACULTY HOLDING RESEARCH APPOINTMENTS. GUIDED BY THE UT INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURE'S A DECADE OF EXCELLENCE (2018-2028) AND GROWING GREATNESS (2025-2030) STRATEGIC PLANS, UT AGRESEARCH HAS ESTABLISHED THE AGRESEARCH STRATEGIC ACTION PLAN (ASAP) AS A ROADMAP TO MEET STATE AND NATIONAL NEEDS. ASAP FOCUSES ON BALANCING A PORTFOLIO OF INTEGRATED, INTERDISCIPLINARY PROGRAMS; CULTIVATING COLLABORATIVE TEAMS; ADVANCING INNOVATIVE CONCEPTS WITH STRUCTURED SUPPORT; AND SUSTAINING RESEARCH CAPACITY THROUGH TARGETED INVESTMENTS. FOUR THEMATIC INTEGRATED PROGRAMS ADDRESS COMPLEX, EMERGING CHALLENGES: UT ONE HEALTH INITIATIVE - A UT SYSTEM-WIDE PROGRAM HOUSED WITHIN AGRESEARCH THAT ADVANCES HUMAN, ANIMAL, PLANT, AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH TO PROMOTE ECONOMIC GROWTH AND ECOSYSTEM RESILIENCE AT LOCAL, NATIONAL, AND GLOBAL LEVELS. PRECISION AND DIGITAL AGRICULTURE - A TRANSDISCIPLINARY EFFORT INCORPORATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, SENSING TECHNOLOGIES (E.G., DRONES AND ROBOTICS), AND DATA ANALYTICS TO ENHANCE PRODUCTION EFFICIENCY, CONSERVE FINITE NATURAL RESOURCES, REDUCE LABOR DEMANDS, AND IMPROVE PROFITABILITY. PROJECTS SPAN PLANT AND ANIMAL SYSTEMS, ENABLING PRODUCERS TO MAKE INFORMED, DATA DRIVEN DECISIONS. AGRICULTURAL GENOMICS AND SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY - A TRANSFORMATIONAL INITIATIVE ADVANCING PRODUCTIVITY AND RESILIENCE IN PLANTS AND ANIMALS THROUGH GENETIC INNOVATION. RESEARCH FOCUSES ON DISEASE AND DROUGHT RESISTANCE, WATER-USE EFFICIENCY, YIELD IMPROVEMENT, AND MITIGATION OF WILDLIFE DAMAGE, POSITIONING TENNESSEE AT THE FOREFRONT OF NEXT-GENERATION CROP AND LIVESTOCK DEVELOPMENT. BIOECONOMY ADVANCEMENT - AN INTERDISCIPLINARY PROGRAM CREATING SUSTAINABLE FUELS, CHEMICALS, AND MATERIALS FROM RENEWA BLE OR STRANDED BIOMASS RESOURCES. FUNDING FROM THE FEDERAL ALLOCATION AND THE CORRESPONDING MATCHING FUND FROM THE STATE ARE USED TO COVER EXPENSES RELATED TO THESE ACTIVITIES. ADDITIONAL FUNDS COME FROM EXTERNAL GRANTS SECURED BY THE RESEARCH SCIENTISTS. APPLIED RESEARCH PROJECTS USING THESE FUNDS TARGET MAINLY LIMITED-RESOURCE PRODUCERS IN THE STATE BUT SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERIES IMPACT THE CITIZEN OF STATE OF GEORGIA, THE COUNTRY, AND THE WORLD.

awards.Description: KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY'S 1890 COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM SERVES YOUTH, FARMERS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES THROUGHOUT THE STATE. OUR EXTENSION PROGRAMMING COVERS AGRICULTURE EDUCATION THROUGH PRODUCTION DEMONSTRATIONS, MONTHLY THIRD THURSDAY THING WORKSHOPS, AND ONE-ON-ONE TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO FARMERS FROM OUR EDUCATORS IN TOPICS SUCH AS SOIL MANAGEMENT, POND MANAGEMENT, CLIMATE-SMART AGRICULTURE, ORGANIC AGRICULTURE, HORTICULTURE, TREE FRUIT CULTURE, APICULTURE, AQUACULTURE, AQUAPONICS, HYDROPONICS, SMALL RUMINANTS, BEEF CATTLE, ETC. OUR EXTENSION DRONE TEAM, IN COLLABORATION WITH OUR REMOTE SENSING RESEARCHERS, IS A POWERFUL RESOURCE FOR FARMERS AND NEXT-GENERATION ORGANIZATIONS THAT SEEK TO TRAIN YOUTH AND UTILIZE MODERN TECHNOLOGY-BASED AGRICULTURE TO MANAGE AGRONOMIC CROPS, CROP PEST AND DISEASE, AND LIVESTOCK HERDS. OUR EXTENSION EDUCATORS PROVIDE KNOWLEDGE AND SUPPORT IN TOPICS RELATED TO HUMAN NUTRITION AND HUMAN HEALTH TO COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE STATE THROUGH VARIOUS AVENUES INCLUDING OUR MOBILE HEALTH UNITS. WORKING IN COLLABORATION WITH HUMAN HEALTH AND NUTRITION RESEARCHERS, THESE EDUCATORS ARE TRAINING STAKEHOLDERS OF ALL AGES HOW TO INCORPORATE NUTRITIOUS AND TASTY FOODS INTO HEALTHY, BUDGET-FRIENDLY DIETS, WHILE ALSO MITIGATING CHRONIC ILLNESSES SUCH AS DIABETES AND HEART DISEASE THROUGH INCREASED PHYSICAL ACTIVITY. OUR 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT STAFF ARE TRAINING YOUTH IN STEM, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, THE ENVIRONMENT, HEALTHY LIFESTYLES, FUTURE CAREERS, AND MENTAL HEALTHCARE. THESE EDUCATORS ARE REACHING SCHOOLS, RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATIONS, 4-H CLUBS, AND OTHER PLACES WHERE THEY CAN ENGAGE YOUTH AND PROMOTE POSITIVE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT APPROACHES. THEY ARE ALSO FORMING STRONG PARTNERSHIPS WITH PARENTS, GUARDIANS, SCHOOLTEACHERS, COACHES, RELIGIOUS LEADERS, ETC., TO ENGAGE YOUTH THROUGH IN-SCHOOL ENRICHMENT, AFTER-SCHOOL PROGRAMS, AND A MULTIPLICITY OF SUMMER CAMPS. OUR COMMUNITY RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT STAFF COLLABORATE WITH LOCAL LEADERS AND ORGANIZATIONS TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITIES THROUGH LEADERSHIP TRAINING, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, WORKFORCE READINESS, LAND RETENTION, AND DISASTER EDUCATION INITIATIVES THAT PROMOTE SUSTAINABLE GROWTH AND RESILIENCE. THEY ALSO BUILD PARTNERSHIPS THAT ENHANCE CIVIC ENGAGEMENT, INCREASE ACCESS TO RESOURCES, AND SUPPORT EQUITABLE ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES ACROSS KENTUCKY COMMUNITIES. ALL OF OUR EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE FUNDAMENTALLY DRIVEN BY THE NEEDS OF OUR LAND-GRANT CLIENTS AND ARE DESIGNED IN RES PONSE TO THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL ISSUES IDENTIFIED IN OUR USDA PLAN OF WORK: 1) AGRICULTURE, ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES; 2) ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL WELL-BEING; 3) FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY; 4) LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT; 5) LIFE SKILL DEVELOPMENT; 6) NUTRITION AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES; 7) SMALL FARM DEVELOPMENT; AND, 8) SUBSTANCE USE RECOVERY AND MENTAL WELLBEING.

awards.Description: KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY'S 1890 LAND-GRANT EXTENSION PROGRAM IS TO SERVE THE NEEDS OF LIMITED RESOURCE AND SMALL FARMERS, AND LOW-INCOME AND SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED RESIDENTS OF THE STATE. THIS SERVICE ENTAILS NEEDS ASSESSMENTS OF OUR FELLOW KENTUCKIANS, COORDINATION WITH 1890 LAND- GRANT RESEARCHERS, AND MEANINGFUL AND TIMELY DELIVERY OF EDUCATIONAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS. EXTENSION PROGRAMS COVER AGRICULTURE EDUCATION THROUGH PRODUCTION DEMONSTRATIONS, MONTHLY WORKSHOPS, AND ONE-ON-ONE SUPPORT TO FARMERS FROM OUR EDUCATORS IN TOPICS INCLUDING SOIL MANAGEMENT, POND MANAGEMENT, CLIMATE-SMART AGRICULTURE, ORGANIC AGRICULTURE, HORTICULTURE, TREE FRUIT CULTURE, APICULTURE, AQUACULTURE, AQUAPONICS, HYDROPONICS, SMALL RUMINANTS, AND BEEF CATTLE. THESE EDUCATORS ARE TRAINING LOW-INCOME STAKEHOLDERS ABOUT NUTRITIOUS AND TASTY FOODS THAT ARE BUDGET FRIENDLY, WHILE MITIGATING CHRONIC ILLNESSES SUCH AS DIABETES AND HEART DISEASE. OUR 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT STAFF ARE ENGAGING YOUTH FROM SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES AND TRAINING THEM IN STEM, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, THE ENVIRONMENT, HEALTHY LIFESTYLES, FUTURE CAREERS, AND MENTAL HEALTHCARE. THESE EDUCATORS ARE REACHING SCHOOLS, RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATION, 4-H CLUBS, AND OTHER PLACES WHERE THEY CAN ACCESS YOUTH TO THE KNOWLEDGE OF ALL THAT 1890 LAND-GRANT PROGRAMS CAN OFFER THEM. THEY ARE FORMING STRONG PARTNERSHIPS WITH PARENTS, GUARDIANS, SCHOOLTEACHERS, COACHES, AND RELIGIOUS LEADERS, TO ENGAGE YOUTH DURING IN SCHOOL AND AFTER-SCHOOL PROGRAMS AND A MULTIPLICITY OF SUMMER CAMPS. OUR EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE FUNDAMENTALLY DRIVEN BY THE NEEDS OF OUR LAND-GRANT CLIENTS THAT ARE EXEMPLIFIED BELOW IN THROUGH THE CRITICAL ISSUES FOUND IN OUR USDA PLAN OF WORK WHICH INCLUDES: 1) LIFE SKILLS DEVELOPMENT. PROGRAMING WILL EXPAND EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH IN STEM/STEAM AREAS TO INCREASE ENROLLMENT OF LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES WHO ARE AT OR BELOW THE POVERTY LEVEL AND WHO QUALIFY FOR SUPPORT SERVICES. 2) NUTRITION AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. PROGRAMS WILL FOCUS ON ENSURING SAFE, NUTRITIOUS, AND HIGH QUALITY SUPPLY OF FOOD FOR ALL. IN ADDITION, THERE IS A COMMON GOAL FOR LAND GRANT INSTITUTIONS TO PROMOTE HEALTH AND SAFETY WITHIN KENTUCKY HOMES AND COMMUNITY ENVIRONMENTS. MOREOVER, PROGRAMS TO COMBAT SOCIAL ILLS, SUCH AS CHILDHOOD OBESITY AND THE OPIOID EPIDEMIC. 3) FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY. EXTENSION AND RESEARCH STRIVE TO REDUCE THE EXTENT OF FOODBORNE ILLNESSES DUE TO CONTAMINATION OF FOOD. PROGRAMS ARE DESIGNED TO TACKLE THE PROBLEM AT THE LEVELS OF PRODUCTION, PROCESSING, AND CONSUMPTION. RESEARCH INCLUDES THE REDUCTION OF RISKS FROM NATURAL AND MANUFACTURED TOXINS IN FOOD. A SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF EFFORT IS PLACED ON THE IMPORTANCE OF SECURING NUTRITIOUS LOCAL FOODS THROUGH ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS. 4) AGRICULTURAL, ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES. RESEARCH-BASED PRACTICES AND TOOLS DELIVERED THROUGH EXTENSION WILL ENSURE CONTINUED PRODUCTIVITY OF OUR PRODUCERS WHILE ENCOURAGING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF SOUND ENVIRONMENTAL PRACTICES AND EFFECTIVE STEWARDSHIP OF NATURAL RESOURCES. PROGRAMS MUST ADDRESS WATER QUALITY, SOIL HEALTH AND CONSERVATION IN ROW- CROP PRODUCTION, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT AND POLLINATOR HEALTH, AQUACULTURE, HORTICULTURE, ORGANIC PRODUCTION, MASTER GARDENERS, AND SUSTAINABLE ANIMAL PRODUCTION AND MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS. PROGRAMS WILL ALSO CONTINUE FOCUSING ON SUSTAINABLE ENERGY AND AGROECOSYSTEM ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE CHANGE.

awards.Description: THE EXTENSION AND OUTREACH COMPONENT OF TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY'S LAND-GRANT MISSION IS CARRIED OUT THROUGH THE COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM IN THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE. TSU EXTENSION PLACES A SPECIFIC EMPHASIS ON REACHING OUT TO ASSIST FARMERS AND PRODUCERS, WORKING COLLABORATIVELY WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE, THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, AND COUNTY GOVERNMENTS. TSU EXTENSION HAS A BROAD REACH, WITH COUNTY EXTENSION AGENTS/EDUCATORS, PROGRAM ASSISTANTS, AND SUPPORT STAFF IN 62 COUNTIES ACROSS THE STATE. THESE COUNTY PERSONNEL RECEIVE TRAINING AND EDUCATIONAL/TEACHING MATERIAL FROM TSU'S 23 CAMPUS-BASED EXTENSION FACULTY/SPECIALISTS. OUR PROGRAM IS ORGANIZED AROUND ADDRESSING CRITICAL ISSUES IN FOUR EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING AREAS: 1) AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES (ANR), WHICH ENHANCES URBAN AND RURAL PROSPERITY BY ASSISTING FARMERS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES IN PRODUCING FIELD CROPS, RAISING LIVESTOCK, MANAGING FORESTLANDS, GROWING FRUIT CROPS, AND TENDING HOME GARDENS, ACTIVITIES THAT PRODUCE FOOD AND ENHANCE THE ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRITY OF THE AGROECOSYSTEM. THE ANR PROGRAM PROVIDES FARMERS WITH A WIDE VARIETY OF RESEARCH-BASED TRAINING PROGRAMS TO ENHANCE THEIR PRODUCTIVITY, FARM PROFITABILITY, AND QUALITY OF LIFE, FOCUSING ON ENTOMOLOGY, FORESTRY, SOIL HEALTH, BIOENERGY, PLANT NUTRITION, HORTICULTURE, DRONE TECHNOLOGY,  ECONOMICS, AGRICULTURAL COMMUNICATIONS, AND ORGANIC AGRICULTURE; 2) FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES, WHICH IMPROVES THE HEALTH AND WELL-BEING OF TENNESSEANS BY PROVIDING PROGRAMS ON COMMUNITY NUTRITION EDUCATION, NUTRITION SECURITY, FAMILY AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT, AND HEALTH EDUCATION; 3) EXTENSION 4-H YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, WHICH FOCUSES ON WORKFORCE PREPARATION, STEM EDUCATION, LIFE SKILLS DEVELOPMENT, YOUTH LEADERSHIP, CITIZENSHIP DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS; AND 4) COMMUNITY RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, WHICH PROVIDES INFORMATION AND EDUCATION ON COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT AND INCLUDES AGRIBUSINESS/ENTREPRENEURSHIP TRAINING FOR FARMERS (MANAGEMENT, BASIC ACCOUNTING, ECONOMIC PRINCIPLES, BUDGETS, WHOLE-FARM PLANNING, LAND ACQUISITION, TAX MANAGEMENT) AS WELL AS TRAINING FOR LOCAL BUSINESSES (BUSINESS PLANNING, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, MODERN MARKETING AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT).

awards.Description: COLLEGE OF DUPAGE WILL CREATE EMPLOYER-ALIGNED SHORT-TERM AVIATION AND UAS CERTIFICATES THAT USE NEW FACULTY, SIMULATION, AND DRONE TECHNOLOGY TO QUICKLY PREPARE STUDENTS FOR HIGH-SKILL AVIATION JOBS

RII TRACK-2 FEC: NATURAL RESOURCE SUPPLY CHAIN OPTIMIZATION USING AERIAL IMAGERY INTERPRETED WITH MACHINE LEARNING METHODS -THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA AND THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA, ANCHORAGE WILL CONDUCT SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH THAT IS RESPONSIVE TO THE NEEDS OF THEIR NATURAL RESOURCE BASED ECONOMIES. SPECIFICALLY, QUESTIONS FROM THE AREAS OF SNOW WATER RESOURCES, WILDLAND FIRE MANAGEMENT, AND ABANDONED OIL WELL MONITORING WILL DRIVE THE RESEARCH AGENDA. THE SCIENTIFIC WORK IS UNITED BY A COMMON SET OF TECHNIQUES FOR ANSWERING QUESTIONS. MOREOVER, THE COMMON APPROACH IS TO: 1) USE UNMANNED FLYING VEHICLES CALLED DRONES TO COLLECT PICTURES AND OTHER MEASUREMENTS. WHILE THE INFORMATION ACQUIRED BY DRONES IS HIGH QUALITY, IT IS ALSO A LARGE AMOUNT OF COMPLEX DATA. 2) TO AID IN THE DATA?S INTERPRETATION AND ADDRESS THE SCIENCE QUESTIONS, WE USE MACHINE LEARNING METHODS THAT TRAIN COMPUTERS TO IDENTIFY PATTERNS IN DATA. COLLECTING DATA USING DRONES AND THE USE OF MACHINE LEARNING ARE CRITICAL SKILLS FOR AMERICA?S FUTURE WORKFORCE. OUR ACTIVITIES ARE ALIGNED WITH CAREER TRAINING THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS WITH LOCAL COMPANIES AND INTERNSHIPS FOR PARTICIPATING STUDENTS. WITH THE EMPHASIS ON INTERNSHIPS, THE FOCUS WILL BE RETENTION, RATHER THAN RECRUITMENT OF STUDENTS. DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION EFFORTS WILL WORK IN TANDEM WITH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT TO ENSURE THAT INDIGENOUS, LOW INCOME, AND RURAL MEMBERS OF OUR JURISDICTIONS ARE INTEGRAL TO THE EFFORTS. IT IS PROPOSED TO USE MACHINE LEARNING (ML) TO PROCESS IMAGERY AND OTHER DATA ACQUIRED BY AUTONOMOUS AERIAL SYSTEMS (UAS). PROCESSED DATA WILL SUPPORT SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT BY PROVIDING A CLEAR MEANS OF TESTING HYPOTHESES. THE THREE AREAS OF NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT TO APPLY THIS APPROACH ARE: 1) SNOW WATER RESOURCES, BECAUSE ENERGY PRODUCTION, AGRICULTURAL OUTPUT, AND ECONOMIC GROWTH REQUIRE IMPROVED ASSESSMENT OF THE NATURAL CAPITAL BANKED IN THE MOUNTAIN SNOWPACK. 2) FIRE MANAGEMENT AND SCIENCE, BECAUSE AN ADVANCED UNDERSTANDING OF THE PHYSICAL AND ECOLOGICAL PROCESSES DRIVING WILDFIRE IS REQUIRED FOR MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT BETTER PROTECT FORESTS AND THE CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE WITHIN THEM. 3) ABANDONED OIL WELL MONITORING, BECAUSE DETECTING AND MAPPING UNCAPPED OR IMPROPERLY SEALED OIL AND GAS WELLS WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL DATA FOR IMPROVED MITIGATION, SITE RECLAMATION, AND HAZARD REMOVAL. THE TEAM BRING TOGETHER THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA AND THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA ANCHORAGE TO CONDUCT LOCALLY RELEVANT RESEARCH. THE LOCAL FOCUS STRENGTHENS THE RELATIONS WITH NEARBY COMMERCIAL INTERESTS TO IDENTIFY QUESTIONS COMMON TO ACADEMIC AND COMMERCIAL ENDEAVORS IN MODERN NATURAL RESOURCE BASED ECONOMIES. ATTENTION IS CALLED TO UAS AND ML AS SKILLS VITAL TO BOTH COMMERCIAL AND ACADEMIC WORK. TO ADVANCE THE NATURAL RESOURCE BASED ADVANCED MANUFACTURING INDUSTRIES OF THE JURISDICTIONS, SPECIAL CONSIDERATION IS GIVEN TO DEVELOPING A WORKFORCE THAT SPANS FROM TWO-YEAR COLLEGE GRADUATES TO JUNIOR FACULTY MEMBERS. THIS AWARD'S PLAN CENTERS ON PAID, CREDIT-BEARING INTERNSHIPS WITH KEY PARTNERS, DRAWING COMMERCIAL INTERESTS INTO THE PROPOSED WORK, AND BRINGING JUNIOR FACULTY TO THE RESEARCH. DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION EFFORTS WILL WORK IN TANDEM WITH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT TO ENSURE THAT INDIGENOUS, LOW INCOME, AND RURAL MEMBERS OF THE JURISDICTIONS ARE AN INTEGRAL PART OF EFFORTS. WITH THE EMPHASIS ON INTERNSHIPS, THE FOCUS WILL BE RETENTION, RATHER THAN RECRUITMENT OF STUDENTS. THE PROJECT ENGAGES WITH DISRUPTIVE TECHNOLOGIES THAT HAVE LONG REACHING CONSEQUENCES FOR WORKERS. TO ADDRESS THE CONSEQUENCES RELATED TO THESE TECHNOLOGIES, THE TEAM ENLISTED THE AID OF A SOCIAL SCIENTIST TO CONDUCT STUDIES EVALUATING THE SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC IMPACTS. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.

THE GEORGIA PLAN OF WORK (POW) ENCOMPASSES A FIVE-YEAR PERIOD BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2025. THE PLAN ADDRESSES MAJOR AGRICULTURAL ISSUES AS WELL AS MANY OTHER PROBLEMS FACING RURAL AND URBAN AREAS, THE ENVIRONMENT, FAMILIES AND YOUTH. GEORGIA'S POW REPRESENTS A COORDINATED EFFORT BETWEEN THE STATE'S 1890 AND 1862 LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS, FORT VALLEY STATE UNIVERSITY (FVSU) AND UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA (UGA), THUS PRESENTING ONE JOINT POW AND ANNUAL REPORT TO USDA. THE JOINT POW INCLUDES CORE PROGRAMS AND TARGETED ISSUES SUCH AS PLANT AND ANIMAL PRODUCTION, COMMUNITY/HOME AND LIFE SKILLS, FOOD SAFETY AND QUALITY, HEALTH AND WELLNESS, SUSTAINABILITY/CONSERVATION AND THE ENVIRONMENT, YOUTH AND FAMILY DEVELOPMENT, URBAN AGRICULTURE, AND EMERGING ISSUES (I.E. AI-POWERED DRONES AND AUTONOMOUS TRACTORS IN AGRICULTURE). USDA FUNDS FOR THESE CORE PROGRAMS SUPPORT STATE-LEVEL CORE AND TARGETED ISSUES FACING GEORGIA CITIZENS. THE GEORGIA PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT IS A MULTISTEP PROCESS THAT IS OPERATIONAL ANNUALLY. THE MODEL INCLUDES A METHOD FOR ASSESSING NEEDS AND IDENTIFYING PROBLEMS. IT ALSO INCLUDES PROGRAM EVALUATION TO DETERMINE IMPACTS OF EXTENSION EDUCATIONAL TRAININGS. THE MODEL WORKS IN UNISON WITH MULTIPLE ADVISORY SYSTEMS AT BOTH COUNTY AND STATE LEVELS. GOALS OF THESE PROGRAMS ARE TO DEMONSTRATE SHORT AND LONG-TERM IMPACTS. STATE FUNDING SUCH AS STATE-MATCH, COUNTY FUNDING, GRANTS AND GIFTS LEVERAGED AS A DIRECT RESULT OF THE WORK IN THIS PLAN AIDS IN CREATING THE GREATEST FINAL IMPACTS. CRITICAL ISSUES ARE RELATED TO ANIMAL PRODUCTION; COMMUNITY, HOME AND LIFE SKILLS; FOOD SAFETY AND QUALITY; PLANT PRODUCTION; SUSTAINABILITY, CONSERVATION AND THE ENVIRONMENT; URBAN AGRICULTURE; AND YOUTH AND FAMILY DEVELOPMENT. USDA FACILITY FUNDING AFFORDED FVSU EXTENSION THE OPPORTUNITY TO COMPLETE ITS COLD VEGETABLE PROCESSING FACILITY. THIS FACILITY IS A COMPLIMENT TO FVSU RESEARCH MEAT PROCESSING FACILITY (ENGAGED IN EXPANSION) AS THEY ARE USED TO ADDRESS CONSUMER DEMAND FOR FOOD AND VALUE-ADDED MARKETING OPPORTUNITIES FOR FARMERS. ALSO, DURING THIS FISCAL YEAR, EFFORTS TO MAXIMIZE RETURN ON INVESTMENT VIA IMPACTS, THE 1890 EXTENSION REGION INSTITUTED A PROJECT TO GATHER PROGRAM DATA ACROSS THE 1890 REGION (ALL 1890 LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITIES) CALLED COMMON MEASURES. awards.Description: IN 2024, SC STATE UNIVERSITY ADVANCED ITS MISSION OF TEACHING, RESEARCH, AND OUTREACH BY DELIVERING IMPACTFUL PROGRAMS ACROSS 32 SOUTH CAROLINA COUNTIES. awards.Description: COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH: FRAMEWORKS: GROWING OPEN ONDEMAND: LEVERAGING UNIFIED COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE (GOODLUCK) -THE ABILITY TO PROCESS LARGE SETS OF DATA ON RESEARCH COMPUTING (RC) PLATFORMS HAS LED TO REMARKABLE ADVANCES IN SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING AND HAS BECOME AN INDISPENSABLE TOOL FOR RESEARCHERS, INDUSTRY PROFESSIONALS, AND STUDENTS. THE IMPORTANCE OF RC PLATFORMS AND TOOLS (AND IN PARTICULAR THOSE INVOLVING AI TECHNOLOGY) HAS BEEN RECOGNIZED BY THE HIGHEST LEVELS OF THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT, AS EVIDENT BY THE NATIONAL AI INITIATIVE ACT OF 2020, WHICH CALLS FOR THE CREATION OF A NATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH RESOURCE (NAIRR). UNFORTUNATELY, FOR MANY INDIVIDUALS, RC USE AND ADOPTION IS HINDERED BY THE COMPLEX WAY IN WHICH THESE RESOURCES ARE ACCESSED. WHILE WEB BROWSERS AND SMART DEVICES HAVE BECOME THE DOMINANT ACCESS MECHANISM FOR REMOTE CONSUMER AND ENTERPRISE COMPUTING SERVICES, THE ADOPTION OF SUCH MECHANISMS HAS LAGGED FOR MANY RC SERVICE PROVIDERS, CREATING AN ACCESSIBILITY GAP THAT IMPEDES FURTHER ADOPTION. OPEN ONDEMAND IS A MATURE, NATIONAL SCIENCE FOUNDATION (NSF) FUNDED, OPEN-SOURCE PLATFORM THAT ENABLES REMOTE WEB ACCESS TO RC SERVICES, THEREBY SIMPLIFYING USE OF THOSE RESOURCES AND FACILITATING COLLABORATION. RC CLIENTS CAN MANAGE FILES AND JOBS, CREATE AND SHARE APPS, RUN GUI APPLICATIONS, AND UTILIZE A TRADITIONAL TERMINAL ALL THROUGH A WEB BROWSER FROM ANYWHERE ON ANY DEVICE BECAUSE IT REQUIRES NO SPECIALIZED CLIENT SOFTWARE AND HAS A SIMPLE INTERFACE THAT IS EASY TO LEARN AND USE. THE OPEN ONDEMAND COMMUNITY HAS BEGUN TO EXPOSE PLATFORM LIMITATIONS AND REQUEST ADDITIONAL FEATURES AND CAPABILITIES, MANY OF WHICH WILL REQUIRE SIGNIFICANT COLLABORATIVE DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS TO IMPLEMENT. FURTHER ADOPTION OF THIS POWERFUL PLATFORM, AND THE RESULTANT SCIENTIFIC ADVANCES, CAN BE ACCELERATED VIA A VARIETY OF INNOVATIONS: (1) CATALOG, PROVIDING CAPABILITIES TO CONCEPTUALIZE, CREATE, MODIFY, SHARE, AND PUBLICIZE APPS; (2) CLASSROOM, FOCUSED ON OPEN ONDEMAND IN EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENTS; (3) CUSTOMIZATION, INVOLVING INNOVATION IN CLIENT INTERFACES AND NEW TECHNOLOGIES; AND (4) COMMUNITY, FACILITATING COMMUNICATIONS AMONG THE COMMUNITY. A CROSS-CUTTING ASPECT OF THE GOODLUCK PROJECT WILL PILOT AND DELIVER INTEGRATED SETS OF TOOLS, DOCUMENTATION, AND TRAINING MATERIALS, WHICH RESEARCHERS CAN SELECT FROM TO CREATE AN ENVIRONMENT TAILORED TO THEIR RESEARCH. INITIAL BENEFICIARIES OF THESE EFFORTS INCLUDE: (1) BIOCHEMISTS UTILIZING CRYOGENIC ELECTRON MICROSCOPY (CRYO-EM) TO IDENTIFY THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS OF VIRAL ACTION; (2) MATERIALS SCIENTISTS DESIGNING NEW ALLOYS FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES; (3) ART DESIGN STUDENTS CREATING NOVEL WORKS VIA THE USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE; AND (4) AEROSPACE ENGINEERS IMPROVING THE PERFORMANCE OF DRONES VIA COMPUTATIONAL FLUID DYNAMICS. IN SUMMARY, THE GOODLUCK EFFORT WILL PROVIDE TOOLS AND PROCESSES THAT ALLOW RESEARCHERS TO MORE EASILY AND EXTENSIVELY UTILIZE OPEN ONDEMAND, AS WELL AS TO ANALYZE AND SHARE THEIR COMPUTATIONAL RESULTS, REGARDLESS OF THEIR ACCESS TO RC RESOURCES OR POSITION IN THE RESEARCH LIFECYCLE. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

awards.Description: FIRE-WUI: COMMUNITY RESILIENCE ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK FOR WILDFIRES USING MULTI-RESOLUTION DIGITAL TWINS -WILDFIRES POSE A GROWING THREAT TO COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE US, PARTICULARLY IN AREAS WHERE HOMES AND NATURAL LANDSCAPES MEET, KNOWN AS THE WILDLAND-URBAN INTERFACE (WUI). EACH YEAR, MORE THAN 60,000 WILDFIRES OCCUR IN THE US, OFTEN RESULTING IN TRAGIC LOSS OF LIFE, DESTRUCTION OF HOMES, AND SEVERE ECONOMIC DISRUPTION. EFFECTIVE WILDFIRE RESPONSE AND PREVENTION EFFORTS ARE HINDERED BY A LACK OF DETAILED, UP-TO-DATE INFORMATION ABOUT VEGETATION AND BUILDINGS IN THESE HIGH-RISK AREAS. TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES, THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK THAT CREATES DETAILED, 3D DIGITAL REPRESENTATIONS, REFERRED TO HERE AS DIGITAL TWINS, OF BOTH NATURAL AND BUILT ENVIRONMENTS. THESE DIGITAL TWINS WILL PROVIDE ACCURATE, LOCATION-SPECIFIC INFORMATION NEEDED TO SIMULATE HOW FIRES SPREAD AND ENABLE THE DEVELOPMENT OF MORE EFFECTIVE MITIGATION STRATEGIES. THE INTELLECTUAL MERIT OF THIS PROJECT INCLUDES THE CREATION OF A GROUNDBREAKING FRAMEWORK FOR GENERATING SCALABLE, MULTI-RESOLUTION DIGITAL TWINS THAT COMBINE DATA FROM SATELLITES, DRONES, AND GROUND SENSORS. BY INTEGRATING AI AND ADVANCED MODELING TECHNIQUES, THE SYSTEM WILL ENHANCE THE UNDERSTANDING OF FIRE BEHAVIOR IN WUI ENVIRONMENTS AND SUPPORT MORE ACCURATE FIRE-SPREAD PREDICTIONS. THIS RESEARCH REPRESENTS A CONVERGENT AND INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH THAT COMBINES GEOSPATIAL SCIENCE, WILDFIRE MODELING, AND DATA ANALYTICS IN NOVEL WAYS STILL UNREALIZED AT THIS SCALE. THE BROADER IMPACTS OF THIS PROJECT ARE SIGNIFICANT. THE DIGITAL TWIN FRAMEWORK WILL HELP IMPROVE COMMUNITY RESILIENCE AND PREPAREDNESS AGAINST WILDFIRES BY PROVIDING FIRST RESPONDERS, PLANNERS, AND POLICYMAKERS WITH THE TOOLS TO MAKE FASTER, DATA-DRIVEN DECISIONS. THE SYSTEM IS DESIGNED TO SCALE NATIONWIDE AND CAN BE ADAPTED TO OTHER TYPES OF NATURAL DISASTERS. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PREPARE THE NEXT GENERATION OF EXPERTS THROUGH INTERDISCIPLINARY EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAMS, INCLUDING NEW COURSES, ONLINE LEARNING MODULES, MENTORSHIP, AND PROFESSIONAL TRAINING DEVELOPED IN COLLABORATION WITH INDUSTRY ORGANIZATIONS. THESE EFFORTS WILL ENSURE A MORE KNOWLEDGEABLE WORKFORCE READY TO CONFRONT THE COMPLEX CHALLENGES OF WILDFIRE MANAGEMENT. THE ?COMMUNITY RESILIENCE ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK AGAINST WUI-FIRES USING MULTI-RESOLUTION DIGITAL TWINS ? (CRAFT)? PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A SCALABLE, DYNAMIC DIGITAL TWIN FRAMEWORK TO SUPPORT WILDFIRE MODELING AND MITIGATION IN THE WUI. CRAFT WILL INTEGRATE HETEROGENEOUS GEOSPATIAL DATA FROM SATELLITE, AERIAL, AND GROUND-BASED PLATFORMS USING AI-BASED SUPER-RESOLUTION, GENERATIVE MODELING, AND QA/QC PROTOCOLS TO CREATE MULTI-RESOLUTION, CONTINUOUSLY UPDATED 3D MODELS. THESE DIGITAL TWINS WILL FEED INTO ENHANCED FIRE-SPREAD MODELS TO IMPROVE PREDICTION ACCURACY AND INVESTIGATE THE TRADE-OFF AMONG RESOLUTION, PERFORMANCE, AND COMPUTATIONAL COMPLEXITY. THE IMPROVED MODELS ARE THEN USED TO EVALUATE MITIGATION STRATEGIES. VALIDATION WILL OCCUR THROUGH TESTBEDS WITH DISTINCT CHARACTERISTICS IN THE U.S. EASTERN AND WESTERN WUI REGIONS. EDUCATIONAL COMPONENTS WILL SUPPORT WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT IN GEOSPATIAL AND WILDFIRE SCIENCES. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.

awards.Description: COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH: FRAMEWORKS: BUILDING THE TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY CITIZEN SCIENCE FRAMEWORK TO ENABLE SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY ACROSS DISCIPLINES -TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY RESEARCH IS ENABLED BY THE AVAILABILITY OF VAST AMOUNTS OF DATA, COLLECTED ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF TEMPORAL AND SPATIAL SCALES, OFTEN IN REAL TIME. ENTIRE FLEETS OF SATELLITES, DRONES AND OTHER DEVICES MONITOR THE EARTH AT EVER-INCREASING RESOLUTION, ADDING TO THE ENORMOUS CORPUS OF MAPS AND METADATA THAT ENABLE SCIENCES FROM GEOLOGY TO BIODIVERSITY. WHILE CITIZEN SCIENCE - OR CROWDSOURCING SCIENCE - HAS BEEN SUCCESSFULLY LEVERAGED OVER THE PAST SEVERAL DECADES TO CLOSE THE ANALYSIS GAP ARISING FROM LARGE AMOUNTS OF DATA, THE SHEER SCALE AND COMPLEXITY OF THESE NEW DATA SETS PRESENTS NEW CHALLENGES. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THESE CHALLENGES THROUGH NOVEL CITIZEN SCIENCE CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE (CSCI) WHERE NEW TOOLS AND TECHNIQUES, INCLUDING TEAMING HUMANS WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), ARE BEING DEVELOPED TO ENABLE RESEARCHERS TO EFFICIENTLY EXTRACT THE BEST RESULTS FROM LARGE AND COMPLEX DATA SETS. THIS EFFORT INCORPORATES MAPPING, MACHINE LEARNING, AND DATA SHARING INNOVATIONS IN BIODIVERSITY, GEOSCIENCE, AND ASTRONOMY RESEARCH AND EXPANDS THE CAPACITY OF RESEARCH COMMUNITIES ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF DISCIPLINES TO USE CITIZEN SCIENCE AS A SUITABLE, OPEN AND SUSTAINABLE RESEARCH METHODOLOGY. THIS PROJECT LEVERAGES NSF-SUPPORTED CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING THE ZOONIVERSE CITIZEN SCIENCE PLATFORM WITH ITS NEARLY THREE MILLION VOLUNTEERS, TO PROVIDE A NOVEL CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE BY: (1) INTEGRATING MAPPING INFRASTRUCTURE INTO ZOONIVERSE TO ACCELERATE ACCURATE PROCESSING AND CURATION OF OFTEN COMPLEX DATA SETS FOR GEOSCIENCE AND BIODIVERSITY PROJECTS; (2) PROVIDING AN INCUBATOR HUB FOR RESEARCHERS AND DEVELOPERS TO DESIGN AND DEPLOY INNOVATIVE CITIZEN SCIENCE PROJECTS WITH A FAST PRODUCTION TURN-AROUND PARTICULARLY FOR AI TRAINING; AND (3) PROVIDING CYBER-PATHWAYS TO EXISTING CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE, CREATING DOCUMENTATION FOR ZOONIVERSE PROJECTS TO RESPONSIBLY DEPOSIT THEIR DATA INTO APPROPRIATE REPOSITORIES, AND FACILITATING WORKSHOPS FOR ZOONIVERSE PROJECT TEAMS TO DEVELOP BEST PRACTICES FOR DATA AND MODEL SHARING. TO ENSURE WIDE DISSEMINATION OF THE NEW CSCI, A STRONG COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE IS ENGAGED AND SUPPORTED THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT EFFORT. THE PROJECT IS LED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA IN COLLABORATION WITH THE ADLER PLANETARIUM AND THE UNIVERSITY OF OXFORD, AS CORE ZOONIVERSE INSTITUTIONS AND ASTROPHYSICS EXPERTISE, AND JOINED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA AND THE FLORIDA MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY WITH EXPERTISE IN BIODIVERSITY, MUSEUM SPECIMEN COLLECTIONS, AND DATA REPOSITORIES, AS WELL AS NORTHERN ARIZONA UNIVERSITY WITH EXPERTISE IN EARTH SCIENCES, MAPPING CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE, AND THE STUDY OF THE ANTARCTICA?S DRY VALLEYS. AS THE LARGEST CITIZEN SCIENCE PLATFORM, AND WITH KEY TOOLS FOR HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP DATA ANALYSIS TASKS, THE ZOONIVERSE IS UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO DEVELOP SKILLS AND BEST PRACTICES TO LOWER THE BARRIER FOR RESEARCH TEAMS TO RESPONSIBLY SHARE DATA AND MODELS. THIS IS CARRIED OUT THROUGH FACT-FINDING AND DEMONSTRATION WITH SEVERAL KEY GROUPS WHO ARE EXEMPLARS IN THE DATA AND MODEL SHARING ECOSYSTEM, INCLUDING GITHUB, THE NATIONAL SCIENCE DATA FABRIC (NSDF), THE GLOBAL BIODIVERSITY INFORMATION FACILITY (GBIF), AND OPEN SCIENCE CHAIN. THIS AWARD REFLECTS NSF'S STATUTORY MISSION AND HAS BEEN DEEMED WORTHY OF SUPPORT THROUGH EVALUATION USING THE FOUNDATION'S INTELLECTUAL MERIT AND BROADER IMPACTS REVIEW CRITERIA.- SUBAWARDS ARE NOT PLANNED FOR THIS AWARD.
